Phainon was a person who smiled a lot, that much everyone in the Holy City knew.

He wasn't just a Chrysos Heir on the path of the Flame-Chase. Nor was he the Deliverer (as a certain prince would call him almost all the time) that was destined to witness the new tomorrow alone. He mingled with the townsfolk easily. Well, Lady Tribios as well (Aglaea was slowly losing her divinity-she's at the stage where she doesn't even know how to talk to children anymore, Castorice had to stay 3 feet away from the population and Mydei…well no explanation was needed there), but there was something about those striking blue eyes and snowy white hair that seems to draw everyone in.

However, whether those smiles were real or not, no one could know. After all, he was shrouded in mystery. No one knows where he came from or how he arrived at Okhema. To the people's knowledge, he's been here long. Time has passed. New generations of Okhemans are now living their carefree lives, playing all sorts of games with their friends. People have come and gone, some friends and others strangers. The new tomorrow was near the horizon.

If only the Boy Saviour could feel happy about it.

“Watch it, Deliverer!” Mydei hissed, jumping to the left as a stray arrow nearly sliced his shoulder. Phainon gave him an apologetic look before grabbing another arrow from the quiver and nocking it carefully. The prince sighed and made his way to his side.

Thankfully, the training grounds were empty, and Mydeimos was glad he had the foresight to clear the area before he and Phainon worked on the Deliverer's archery skills. Which wasn't going…so well, as evidenced by the fact he almost pierced his heart. Not that he was worried or anything, but he really wasn't in the mood to be sent to Thanatos’ embrace and come back to life.

Phainon had his tongue stuck out, eyes scrunched as he focused on nocking the arrow to the bow... and failing miserably. Oh, Titans.

This was wonderful. This was fine. Fine. It could be worse.

Mydei tsked in disapproval and flexed his fingers, resisting the massive urge to pinch his nose and sigh. The man thankfully took the hint and handed the bow. “Too slow there, dear Deliverer, the enemy would have killed you ten times over. You need to be faster in getting your weapon ready.”

“Hey!” Phainon huffed, puffing his cheeks and folding his arms. “We've only been at this thrice. I can't become an expert overnight. Have some patience, Mydei.”

‘If only someone could give some to me,’ Mydei thought grimly. Then again, this whole thing was his idea, wasn't it?

Phainon was good with a sword and greatsword. He was one of the best, keeping up with him in a fight. The way he swung his weapon with deadly precision and blocked most blows that would've shattered an ordinary person's arms. But when it came to using long-range gear, his eyesight suddenly decided not to work. At least that's what Mydei thinks.

He couldn't always rely on his sword. Sure it was forged by Chartonus to ensure it never gets destroyed in battle, but what if he loses it at some point? Of course, the possibility of that was very low, but it wasn't zero. Learning a wide array of weapons is always good for improving one's skills and guaranteeing survival on the field.

Mydei mostly fought with his fists, using his gauntlets to punch a hole in the enemy, and he usually never found himself using anything else. However, his mother taught him the ways of the blade and archery, and when things looked desperate he'd grab the nearest weapon and use it. The Kremnoan Detachment largely used swords and shields and preferred to use only those. He knows he can't make them change their mind, and everyone knows who the Prophecy is referring to. ‘The one who will get to see the new tomorrow.’

But this was proving to be more difficult than he previously thought.

Mydei handed the bow back to Phainon. “There you go. Now try to hit the target in front of you and not me. I don't want to die again after yesterday's skirmish.”

“Aye aye teach!” Phainon replied, giving him a mock salute and a wink. Mydei merely glared at him and rolled his eyes. He heard a soft peal of laughter before the swordsman positioned his arms properly and drew the arrow back, one eye closed. At least he managed to nail that consistently.

“Remember,” Mydei started to say, standing behind him, “relax your muscles and calm down. You're not surrounded by enemies. You're only training and therefore, you don't need to be tense.”

“Kind of hard not to be,” Phainon whispered. “I've messed this up way too many times for my liking.”

“Doesn't everyone make mistakes?”

“Does everyone have the time to be here teaching?”

Ah. Mydei shook his head. Yes, he had things to do, and he had a squad to lead in two days with Hyacine to check up on some scholars and warriors who were stationed in a place that he doesn't quite remember (though it was somewhere beyond the Grove and Hyacine knows where, and Mydei trusts her judgment), so he should be preparing for that. All in all, his schedule was packed.

Yet, he still made room for this because he wanted the other Heirs to broaden their horizons when it came to battle tactics and, subsequently, their methods of fighting. Mydei does agree with Aglaea's methods most of the time, and she does acknowledge that brute strength is the solution to half of their problems, but…

Well, deep down he knew- everyone knew- he wasn't going to be in Okhema forever. He and his people were here as refugees. But one day the Kremnoans would have to return home to fight the perilous Black Tide. Nikador would have to be dealt with, and the Coreflame would have to be retrieved. And once that's done he’ll have to follow the prophecy and start his Flame-Chase journey. And until then, he wanted Okhema to be prepared. He wanted his friend to be prepared. That's why he was doing this.

He wasn't going to say that out loud though.

“Well, I have the time now,” Mydei said instead, wincing at how harsh his words came out. Phainon, thankfully, looked undeterred. He silently hoped he hadn’t kept the man waiting for so long with his internal monologue- now how embarrassing would that be? “And you aren’t the only person I’m teaching this to, Deliverer. You just happened to be my first victim.”

Phainon laughed again, this time sounding brighter than before. Now that sounded much better. Lowering his arms, he teased, “Come on now, Mydeimos, you and I know the truth. Who are you trying to lie to? Yourself? There’s no one here to pretend to.”

“It’s called dignity, dear Phainon,” Mydei hissed and grabbed his arms and raised them again. “And just because I chased everyone away won’t stop one random fool from waltzing in here. And you know I can’t lock the doors.”

“Because that would look suspicious.”

“Phainon–!”

“🎶No matter how much you may think it, you can’t kill me 🎶”

…That was infuriatingly true. Mydei groaned when he taunted him with his stupid sing-song voice. He twisted Phainon’s arms, ignoring the surprised yelp that came out of his mouth, and pointed him to the target. “Let the arrow fly.”

“Er, you sure?”

“Trust me,” Mydei smirked. “I’d never waste a precious arrow. Now let it go.”

And Phainon did just that. After Mydei took a step back, he released his hold on the shaft and cried out in joy when it made its mark right at the center. The prince felt his smirk grow wider.

He turned his head to look at him. “So, you think you can hit the spot on your own now?”

“I mean…wait what am I saying? Of course, I can!” Phainon exclaimed, blue eyes shining in determination as he grabbed another arrow and nocked it as fast as he could. Mydei peered over his shoulder and was satisfied that it didn’t almost fall through his fingers this time. He straightened his back, pulled the string back, and planted his feet firmly onto the ground. He kept his hand steady, one eye closed, and took a deep breath. Mydei raised a brow, relieved that the idiot was finally easing up a little, and took a step forward. He didn’t say anything, but nothing needed to be said.

And, a few seconds later, Phainon let the arrow soar…

Right into the middle.

Silence. Then…

“BULLSEYE!!!!!!!!”

Phainon pumped his fists into the air, laughing so hard he nearly fell to the ground, had it not been for Mydei to catch him at the nick of time. He couldn’t bring himself to be mad at the egghead for screaming like that. Those cheerful-sounding giggles were infectious– even Mydei himself wasn’t fully immune to it. He doubted he ever would be. He still scolded him though.

“Be a little more careful, would you? I’m not going to be here for a week, and I’d hate to find your dead body here when I return.”

“Oh, me- my- Mydei,” Phainon gasped between laughs, his chest rising and falling rapidly, “Yo-you re-a-lly thin-k I’m gon-n-a die th-at eas..eas-i-ly?”

“From the way you look, yes. You’re going to choke on your spit if you don’t quit it right now.”

“We-well, good luck try-na…st–op me!”

Mydei sighed loudly. There was no way he was going to stop him, and if he wanted to try, he’d be subjected to his flailing limbs smacking him everywhere. It’s better to let it run its course.

It only took a mere five minutes before the laughter died out, replaced by him heaving, stray giggles escaping his mouth once in a while. And all the while Mydei’s eyes never left him. After all, how could they? It was like he thought earlier-Phainon’s joy was contagious to anyone.

But what he didn’t expect was that small, crooked smile to appear on his face as he stared at him from the ground. That smile that he saw him rarely wear. The smile, dare he say, was reserved only for him. It was that kind of smile you would know was genuine and not a mask to hide anything. It was raw, real, and it was no secret that Phainon was a man who wore his heart on his sleeve. He sucked in a sharp breath the moment he laid eyes on it.

Phainon raised a hand, and Mydei took it, helping him up to his feet. They didn’t let go, and ‘Snowy’ squeezed his palm carefully. “Thanks, Mydei. I…didn’t think I’d ever need to learn to use other weapons. I’m so used to using my sword all the time, it never crossed my mind that I might not have it on me all the time. And I’m still learning to use my fists,” he joked at the end.

“And that’s why I always tell you that gauntlets are far superior than any other weapon,” Mydei retorted, punching him in the chest. “And that’s also why I tell you to wear the training ones that Chartonus made for you before you decide to have a fistfight with me. You know mine are sharp.”

“Yeah, yeah, next time I will.”

“We’ll see about that.”

“Now, don’t you have troops to prepare and a certain healer to talk to?”

“Dodging the claims, are we?”

“Not at all. Just reminding you that you have your hands full, and the Curtain-Fall Hour is nearly upon us.”

“...Shit,” Mydei nearly yelled, checking the time on the wall. Sure enough, it was nearing six, and he promised Hyacine he’d meet her at 6:10. She was waiting for him at the market. Well, there was no time to lose now, was there?

Phainon chuckled upon seeing his face and nudged him gently. “Go. I’ll take care of cleaning up. I owe you one for taking your time to teach me.”

That was all the confirmation Mydei needed before taking off. The “Stay safe!” doesn’t go unheard either.

The scouting mission took a lot out of Mydei. Never in his immortal life has he ever felt so tired after one battle. And it wasn’t just him feeling those effects either.

The Black Tide. Everyone in Amphoreus knew of its existence. It corrupted the minds of the people, driving them mad to the point of insanity. Once it digs its ugly claws into your brain and stays there for a long period of time, there’s no coming back. That’s what he, Hyacine and the soldiers were up against.

They had to slay their comrades. Their friends. The people that they’ve known for years.

He witnessed countless men kill the people they love, holding them in their arms until Death took them away. He saw the fear in his people’s eyes, despite war being a familiar song to them. The worst was Hyacine. The poor girl was doing her best to heal everyone, both friend and foe, and Mydei saw how it was draining her. He had to drag her out of there before she was exhausted both physically and mentally. Almost all the scholars didn’t make it…

They were making their way back to Okhema with the survivors-it wasn’t the best idea to go to the Grove just yet, though Mydei had sent a messenger to tell Anaxa what happened, and to tell him Hyacine was safe. The light rays were gently piercing the inky black sky, which meant they were close to the Holy City. They set up camp for now and he was sitting on the log while the others rested in the makeshift tents. They all deserved it after the horrors they witnessed.

Mydei stoked the fire with the stick, his mind wandering to the battle. He fought the Black Tide before, when he and the detachment journeyed out of Castrum Kremnos after his father’s death. Aglaea has sent him and Phainon to ward it off several times. He was no stranger to it. But today was different. Those people were mad, but their bodies didn’t bear the signs of corruption. They never got the chance to fully transform because they arrived early. Hearing the sound of blood squirting out of their wounds and the smell of burnt human flesh was…it was sickening .

He has no doubt that Aglaea now knows of what happened. He’ll still have to tell her about it, but at least he could leave out the gory details. The fact that he himself is feeling queasy, and he’s the Crowned Prince of a civilization that was bathed in blood and honor is saying a lot. He’s grateful they didn’t lose anyone in his squad today. He already had to be the bearer of bad news and tell the families that their son or daughter was forever lost to the Black Tide.

Mydei sighed and took a bite of his pomegranate. He was going to stoke the fire again when he heard the rustling of fabric and saw cotton candy pink hair and bright turquoise eyes pop outside of a tent. A second later Hyacine crawled outside and stood up, tilting her head at him, those eyes glittering in the light and her arms clenched by her sides. ‘Oh, Hyacine,’ he thought.

He didn’t have to say anything. He gestured for her to come with his hand, and that’s all she needed before she all but ran towards his side, sitting down and bringing her legs up to bury her face between them, letting out tiny sobs that Mydei had no doubt she had been suppressing for so long. He placed his hand on her shoulder and squeezed it. Thankfully, he didn’t have his gauntlets on, lest he accidentally tear a small piece of fabric with those sharp claws. “Hyacine…”

“They’re dead,” Hyacine wailed, sniffing and wiping her eyes. “All of them are gone ‘De, and I couldn’t save them. No matter what I did or tried to do, I couldn’t get the effects of the Tide out of them.”

“Not everyone can be saved, especially those who are consumed by the Black Tide and you know it. But don’t let today make you underestimate your abilities as a healer.”

“But those men could’ve been saved !” yelled Hyacine, finally looking at him with tears streaming down her eyes. They were red and puffy from crying earlier. Now that Mydei took a good look at her, he saw just how messed up she was right now. Her bright pink hair looked dull even in the warm light of the fire and sticking up in all directions, her clothes were disheveled (and Mydei was well aware that she loved to keep all her clothes including pajamas ironed and pressed), and right now she was breaking down right under his arm.

But, what did she mean by when she said those men could’ve been saved?

“The Black Tide hadn’t fully taken them away,” Hyacine started to say softly, and Mydei had to strain his ears to hear what she was saying. “They had only been affected for a mere five minutes. There was enough time to bring them out of its influence. But…for some unexplained reason the tide was acting like a parasite-well, it is one but it somehow managed to take root in their minds and bodies so fast, they didn’t have time to transform. That’s why when we fought them they looked like their actual selves. The Black Tide has become more relentless, and I…”

She placed a hand over her mouth. “I saw it happen to someone I know. A fellow scholar that I’m good friends with. Her name was Lydia, a smart bird as everyone called her. She always helped out the younger students, and even came to aid me several times at the Twilight Courtyard. She…she begged me to kill her, saying that she didn’t want to hurt anyone. I told her to quit it and let me save her, and as I focused on healing her wounds, I hadn’t noticed that she stole the knife from the nurse near me and before I knew it, she… she… ”

Hyacine’s fingers were wrapped tightly around her pant leg, turning her knuckles red. Mydei gently pried them off. He was at a loss for words. What should he say? What could he say? No words of comfort would be able to heal the wound that was inside her right now. Losing a best friend…it’ll hurt. It’ll hurt so bad, sometimes even driving you to the brink of insanity.

Mydei wrapped his arm around her shivering frame and pulled her into a side hug, and almost immediately she buried her head into the soft fabric. He exhaled slowly, rubbing her arm gently. “Hyacine, I know it hurts. It hurts more than we ever realize. But I need you to listen to me.”

He waited for a response, and when he felt that tiny head nod against his body, he continued to talk. “I’ve lost many of my closest friends before I arrived at Okhema. These five people helped me take my revenge against my father and lead the Kremnoan Detachment to the Holy City. Along the way, they died. One by one, they dropped like flies. When my last friend perished -the person whom I considered as a brother-I felt the world stop. I felt like the wind was sucked out of my lungs.”

Mydei closed his eyes, those memories he buried deep in his mind rising to the surface. Hephaestion, Perdikkas, Leonnius, Ptolemy, Peucesta. He vowed that their names would never be forgotten by history. So long as he lives, the people who sacrificed themselves will always be remembered. His friends would always be remembered by him. It wasn’t fair that fate took them all away from him. That one thought had plagued his mind over and over again, especially once Hephaestion died. That was the day he lost everything. He was at his lowest point after that. But he kept pushing forward for their sakes. He didn’t want their deaths to be in vain. That one thought pierced through the dark fog in his mind. It still hurts, even to this day, but as long as he never forgot and honored them every day, that was enough.

“It took me a while to recover from the aftershock of everything, but once I did, I reminded myself that they weren’t truly dead. A person only dies once their name is no longer uttered in this world. If there are people who can carry on their legacy, they will live on, even if they are now with Thanatos. Lydia will live in your heart, and she will be remembered by her friends. By you, her close friend. Grief is a fickle thing, and it always feels like someone is prying your heart out of your chest. Those wounds take time to heal, and sometimes they may never.”

“I know,” Hyacine whispered. “It…wouldn’t be the first time. But, when I find myself like this, I wonder, how long will I be like this? How long will the pain and agony stay inside and eat me up before I’m back on my feet?”

“There’s no answer to that,” Mydei replied, staring at the fire. “Some heal faster than others. Some may heal completely. Others will have the scars lingering in their hearts. But no matter the case, healing isn’t a linear process. There’s no definitive time, and that’s ok. What matters is that during that time you never forget them, and hold onto the memories you’ve made over the years, whether they be good or bad.”

Hyacine let out a tiny giggle, scooting back a little to look at him. “I never knew the Crown Prince of Kremnos was a wise guy. Ahhhh, not that I’m saying Kremnoans aren’t wise! Er, wait, what am I saying? I’m so sorry! I’m not trying to offend you or anything, De-!”

Mydei laughed. “Calm down,” he said, ruffling her hair. “I’m not offended in any way. Well, if it were Phainon then yes, but not you.”

She laughed again. “You and Phainon really like each other, huh?”

“He can keep up with me in battle and we have each other’s back, that’s all.”

“That’s all?”

“You’ve gotten more bold, haven’t you?” Mydei smirked. Hyacine merely rolled her red eyes. “A few months ago you wouldn’t have said anything.”

“I learn from the best.”

“Anaxa?”

“Both of you.”

Mydei chuckled and grabbed the stick to stoke the fire. They stayed silent, save for Hyacine’s occasional sniffling and tiny sobs. Only time could heal those scars now, and he hoped he got to her.

He heard her yawn and saw her eyes droop. Laughing quietly, he pulled her into a more comfortable position and let her head rest on his side. “Sleep,” Mydei said. “You’re tired. It couldn’t have been easy, healing everyone. Close your eyes and rest.”

“Will you be here?” Hyacine said in a low voice. “Until it is day break?”

Mydei cracked one of his rare smiles. “Of course.”

And sleep Hyacine did. The smile never left his face even after she was out like a light, and he grabbed another pomegranate from the bag. Hephaestion, Perdikkas, Leonnius, Ptolemy, Peucesta.

Even after he is long gone, they will be recorded in the history books and stored within the libraries of Castrum Kremnos. At least, the will once the city is no longer covered in ruins. His heart warmed at the thought. He took one more glance at Hyacine and shook his head- It appeared his words did not just comfort the healer.

Finally, finally they were back in Okhema. The sun greeted them as the Entry Hour had started, and everyone was relieved to be back home.

They took the back route to avoid the people at the market. No one had the heart to break the news to anyone just yet, Mydei included, and Aglaea thankfully agreed with the sentiment. Furthermore, she reassured him that she’d tell the families herself with Anaxa and told him to go rest.

So, he dropped Hyacine to her room (“No, you can fuss over me and the others later once you’ve rested,” he told her when she looked hesitant. “Let your assistants handle everything for once. That’s why you have them, right?) and made his way to the kitchen. So what if he was bone-tired and felt like collapsing on his bed? Mydei loved pomegranates to death, but that sure wasn’t enough to stave off the hunger. He needed a proper meal.

Mydei opened the doors, mentally going through his list of foods he could make without consuming so much time when he noticed two things. Two really strange things. One could even say he witnessed a paradox at that very moment.

On the table was a plate. A plate that held a stack of blueberry pancakes topped with strawberries, syrup and a bit of whipped cream. He knew the plate was for him because it was placed in the corner where he usually sat when he and the other Chrysos Heirs ate their meals together. It was usually Mydei who cooked for the others, so it was a bit surprising to find breakfast waiting for him on the table.

But what surprised him the most was the person behind the stove, humming a tune under his breath and bouncing under his feet. The man whom everyone knew couldn’t cook. The man who almost burned down this very kitchen the last time he tried.

“Phainon?!”

The man yelped, nearly tossing the pan in his hand and held it out like a weapon, pointing it menacingly at the intruder who dared make their way to the Heir’s private room. Mydei raised a brow and scoffed when he saw the man look surprised…and a little sheepish, like he wasn’t expecting him to come back so early.

“Ahhhhhh….Mydei!” Phainon exclaimed, turning off the stove and grabbing another plate stacked with pancakes-this time strawberry with little blueberries and peaches scattered on the top with a small slice of butter, syrup and cream-and setting it on the table. “What-what a surprise! I wasn’t expecting you to arrive back here this early. Aglaea told me you’d be here at around 10:00.”

“Well, here I am now,” Mydei said drily, taking his seat. He inspected every inch and corner of his pancake and was satisfied-and impressed, very impressed that there wasn’t a single cake that was burnt. “How many tries did this take you?”

“Three,” Phainon chirped happily and slid into the seat opposite to him. “I followed your recipe to a tea, and the first two times the batter came out a little too watery, and the third was way too thick. I just used some milk to loosen it a little and voila. The others said they were going to eat a little late, and since I was hungry and heard you guys were coming today, I figured I’d surprise you.”

Mydei started to remove his gauntlets. “Well, I’ll have to admit that you did, Deliverer. This is actually quite a nice surprise.”

“I’m glad you like it. And, uhm…I don’t know if you want to talk about…it, but I heard what…happened.”

“Aglaea?”

“Yeah. Poor Hyacine,” Phainon said sadly. “She got overwhelmed fast. I can’t blame her for it. Even the most seasoned warriors would’ve faltered that day. Even experienced healers such as herself.”

“She’s still young,” said Mydei, cutting into his breakfast and taking a bite. Light, fluffy and airy with rich flavors. Was this the same Phainon who burnt an omelet two weeks ago? How did he become a master chef so fast? He figured he’d ask him later. “It took me a bit of convincing to get her to rest and let the other healers take over. She needed a mental break more than a physical one.”

He was glad no one knew of her breakdown-that was their little secret.

“I’ll go visit her later once she’s rested,” Phainon said, and reached to hold Mydei’s arm. “I can imagine it mustn't have been easy for you as well. You’re going to rest after eating, right?”

“I don’t have anything else to do, other than visit the infirmary later for a checkup, but that’s after Hyacine wakes up. So yes, I’ll take a nap and wake up for lunch.”

“That’s good.” Phainon shot him a smile-that damn, heart melting smile that always made him feel…something. Does the Deliverer know that has an effect him? “I can see it affected you a bit as well. I know Hyacine looks up to you in her own way, and I’m…thankful that you were there for her.”

“There’s no need for that,” Mydei sighed, taking another bite of his pancakes. Their hands stayed entwined on the table. “I did what I had to do, and the girl desperately needed someone to talk to and some shut-eyes.”

“‘I did what I had to do.’ Sure, keep telling me and yourself that.”

“Shut up before I punch you, Deliverer.”

“You wouldn’t dare 🎶.”

“...Shut up and finish eating. We’ll settle this on the training field later.”

“Oooh, is that a challenge? Also, how am I supposed to eat with my mouth shut?”

“Phainon of Aedes Elysiae-”

“Relax!” Phainon laughed, squeezing his hand. “You know I’m just teasing you. You’re more tired than I thought. Eat and rest, and then in the evening we’ll have a small spar after your check up. That sound good?”

And oh, it does.

Chapter Notes

So I said this chapter was gonna be on the shorter side...heh. Eheheh.

I'm still brainstorming an idea for the next chapter and it's gonna be delayed cause I got a really bad cold 🤧. But hey, MORE PHAIDEI CONTENT!!!

I fixed up any errors that may be there, but I will double-check once more in the morning

“How… many Titankin have… you slayed?”

“78. You?”

“...65.”

“Looks like you’re losing your touch, Deliverer,” Mydei smirked, wiping the blood smeared across his face. Beside him, Phainon shot him a half-hearted glare, panting heavily. The smirk only grew on his face.

The abominations came out of nowhere near the outskirts of Aidonia, and it was only thanks to Aglaea’s golden threads that she was able to identify the sudden threat and dispatch him and the Deliverer to deal with it. They were quite far away from Okhema, so they would have reached the Holy City in about three days. It was thanks to Lady Trianne's Century Gate that they were able to arrive in time. It was always better to deal with the problem before it became a major problem.

At first, the duo thought they alone would be enough to deal with them, and they still did.

However, they were so close to giving up.

They split up to cover more ground. They were Okhema’s strongest warriors- they could handle battling a small army on their own if they wanted to. It was Mydei this time who challenged Phainon, and the latter gladly accepted, that familiar fire burning in those azure blue eyes. Now, he was almost- almost regretting the whole thing. Regretting it because, while their intel was right and there were monsters almost everywhere, they never, in a million years, expected a whole ass army of them! An army that could rival in size Castrum Kremnos’ Elite Guard!

They severely underestimated the number of Titankin. Splitting up was the right call to make to deal with the two waves that were coming at them, but even then, there were a lot of them that, at one point, Mydei thought it would’ve been a little nicer if they had brought a few soldiers with them. He wasn’t sure how well Phainon was faring in this mess. They agreed to meet at the center of the courtyard once they’d all been taken care of. Mydei was the last to arrive, and he saw Phainon sitting down on the steps, slumped over, his greatsword planted into the ground. His eyes were closed. Mydei nudged him gently to get his attention.

After Phainon had woken up (“I wasn’t sleeping! Just resting my eyes is all.”) they were wondering what the fuck was really going on. The Titankin weren’t intelligent creatures- they were built for was to destroy whatever was in their path. Also, from the way they were fighting, it looked like they knew they were going to come. They were anticipating their arrival. Mydei was about to voice out this theory when he saw something that made his blood turn cold.

Now, Mydei bore several scratches on his arms and chest, but those would heal themselves in a few minutes. Nothing that his curse couldn’t fix. Phainon, on the other hand, looked like he went to the forest to maul a bear. His head hung low, and he was breathing laboriously. His sleeves were torn and bloodied, and he had a huge gash across his left cheek, nearly reaching his eye. Dirt covered his cape and boots, and…

Was that a…was that a stab wound on his stomach!?

“Deliverer!” Mydei nearly yelled, hovering over him. With the way Phainon was hunched over, he didn’t notice his blood-soaked shirt until he shifted a bit to the side to reveal a huge gash across his stomach. And, oh, that was quite a bit of blood.

At once, he forced the other to lie down (thankfully without much complaining, except for a little whine that he paid no mind to) and carefully tore the fabric to inspect the wound. Titan’s above, he should’ve seen this coming! The way he was breathing, the sweat covering his forehead, and his fucking posture of all things! Did the man have some sort of death wish?

“Are you an idiot?” Mydei snarled, ripping some fabric from his cape and wrapping it around the wound to staunch the bleeding. It didn’t look like the cut was deep, but he wasn’t a healer. All he knew was basic first aid, and that wasn’t going to help him now with all that golden blood spilled everywhere. “Phainon, answer me! Why didn’t you say anything before you little HKS!?”

“I…I thought,” Phainon rasped, wincing when Mydei tied the fabric securely to the gash. “I thought I could…handle it. I…didn’t want to m…make you wor..ry.”

“Well, didn’t that work out well!?” roared Mydei. This…this manchild actually thought hiding a cut that large that could be fatal was a good idea? Because he didn’t want to worry anyone? Then it dawned upon him, and a strong wave of anxiety washed over him. He had no idea how long Phainon had been waiting for him. He had no idea how long he had been bleeding for.

Oh, fuck. “When we get back to Okhema, I’m going to make sure I end you myself after you’re healed, bring you back from Thanatos’ embrace and kill you again.”

Phainon laughed, spitting blood everywhere. “Now is–n’t that a…bit of a-an over-k-ill?”

“Not in my eyes. If you had said something earlier, we could’ve made it back to the city. Instead you made me talk about the fucking Titankin! ”

Mydei was mad. Furious. Livid. Everything . But years of practice had helped him rein in that anger and channel it into something more productive. Right now, screaming at Phainon wasn’t going to help anyone. Getting him back to Okhema was his first priority, and he hoped Hyacine had had enough rest to treat him.

Phainon wheezed, grabbing Mydei’s forearm with such strength it startled him for a second, “Geez, you-you’re no fun, aren’-aren’t ya?”

“Save your breath,” Mydei hissed. “Focus on staying alive. You’ll have the time to yap all you want once you’re healed.”

“I-I don't…yap that mu..ch.”

The blood soaked almost completely through the fabric, and Mydei sucked in a sharp breath. He had to get him out of here, and fast. “Phainon, I'm going to carry you back to the city, and until we get there do not close your eyes. Do you understand me?”

“I..don't know,” Phainon gasped and let out a tiny cry when Mydei secured another piece of fabric to his abdomen. “I..uh, My-dei?”

“What did I say about talking?”

“I…I th-think I mig-might…pass out.”

“...WHAT!? Goddamnit, Phainon, stay with me! Don’t you dare close your eyes!” Mydei got up and carefully hoisted the swordsman into his arms, being careful not to accidentally scratch him with his gauntlets. Making sure he had a good grip on him, he grabbed Phainon’s greatsword, tossed it behind his shoulder, and yelled for a Century Gate, ignoring the blood that was splattered everywhere on his body.

“He’s going to be alright, De,” Hyacine said, double-checking the gauze wrapped tightly around Phainon’s torso and patted his arm. “You know he’s been through worse.”

“That doesn’t make it any better,” Mydei replied, his eyes never leaving Phainon’s sleeping form. After he brought him back, he went to his room to take a bath (under Hyacine’s orders-he didn't want to leave his side, but she wouldn't let him near the man until he had cleaned up..) “He didn’t say a word about it. Not even a single word, and we counted the number of Titankin we took down. He even laughed, Hyacine! And when I asked him why, he said he, and I quote, ‘I thought I could handle it. It wasn’t a huge wound, so I assumed I could walk it off.’ ”

Ok, so those weren’t his exact words, but that was what he said!

“That…does sound like Phainon alright,” said Hyacine, letting out a sigh. “Regardless, I’ve done everything I can for him. He should wake up in an hour or two, but I can’t guarantee that. He…he lost quite a bit of blood. If you hadn’t managed to staunch the bleeding in time…”

Mydei shuddered. That was one thought he did not want to think about. Phainon was safe, and that was all that mattered.

“I’ll write up a report to Lady Aglaea,” Hyacine continued to say, summoning her pen and pad. “I’m pretty sure she’ll want to know how our Deliverer is faring, and I’ll bring his medicine and some herbs to help replenish his fluids. I also have some other patients to tend to, so it’ll take me a while to get back here. In the meantime, can I entrust you to look after him?”

“Of course,” he instantly replied.

“Thank you. Oh, and do remember to call me if anything happens, though I doubt anything would. He’s well past the danger zone. Thank you once again, De.” And with that, she made her way out of the room, but not before he called out to her.

“Is something wrong?”

“No, just…I told you rest was the key now, didn’t I?”

Hyacine stared at him, dumbfounded for a few seconds before giggling. “It sure was! I think you should open a clinic here for the Chrysos Heirs. You’re really good at listening and giving out advice. You might even make quite a bit of money, not that you need it, considering you’re a prince.”

“A prince of a nation that is now in ruins and is somewhere in Amphoreus," Mydei said drily. "Plus, I have my own duties here, remember?”

“Yeah, yeah, I know De, just pulling your leg is all. Alright then, I’ll see you later.”

Once Hyacine was out of the room, did Mydei truly let himself relax. He unfolded his arms, grabbed the chair nearby and a book Hyacine had left for him, and sat down beside the bed. Phainon was still unconscious, and Hyacine did say it’d take around an hour for him to wake up…

Stealing a glance at the clock, Mydei sighed. He had time to kill, he might as well read the book- something about Mnestia and Cerces’ relationship and wait for the Boy Saviour to open his eyes.

And so, he waited.

And waited…

….

….

…….

This was going to take forever, wasn't it?

Mydei groaned, setting the book on his lap and buried his face into his arms. If Phainon were awake he'd be teasing him like hell. “What? Does the Crown Prince need teaching on patience? You're more impatient than a Dromas waiting for its lunch,” he'd say. But he isn't awake. And the clock wasn't doing much to help him either with its constant, annoying ticking. He had too much energy in his bones despite being utterly exhausted. Should he go for a jog around the city?

'No, not a good idea.’ Hyacine would murder him if she found the room empty, and it would be better for Phainon to wake up with someone near him, in case he needs help remembering why he was in the infirmary. Maybe he could strangle him awake and-

On second thought, maybe he should open that clinic and talk to himself in front of a mirror everyday away from prying eyes. He heard that self-therapy was the new trend these days.

Mydei groaned again and shifted a little in his chair. His right hand found itself playing with Phainon’s hair and he stilled, for a few seconds before he sighed and continued carding his fingers through the locks. He grabbed the book from his lap and flipped through the pages. What surprised him was how invested he slowly became in the story. He wasn’t a guy to read romance novels, no matter if they were real or fictional. He’s also a person who detests reading poetry, yet he has some in his personal library in Kremnos for his friends. Especially Ptolemy, the sap adored reading those kinds of tales.

…He really does miss those idiots at times. At least they were resting peacefully in the Sea of Souls.

He was halfway through the book- at the part where Mnestia was going to confess their love to the Reason Titan-when Mydei felt something stir beneath his hand. He set the book aside and saw Phainon slowly blink his eyes. The man groaned and shielded his eyes from the sudden light from the window, muttering something under his breath. Mydei drew the curtains and made his way back to his side. He heard a tiny wine escape from Phainon’s mouth, and he rolled his eyes, whispering the words “such a puppy,”  before sitting back down on the chair and massaging his scalp. Phainon let out a hum in approval and turned his head to face him, eyes half-closed. “My..Mydei?” he rasped.

“It’s me,” Mydei replied. “How do you feel?”

“Hurts…everywhere. Stomach…argh, the skin -”

“Don’t scratch the area,” Mydei nearly yelled. “Hyacine took a while to bandage that wound. It’s going to feel itchy for a while, but don’t touch it. Understood?”

Phainon hummed. “What…happened to m-me?”

“What do you remember?”

“We were…fighting the Titan..kin near Aidonia. We had to…split up because th..there were so many of them. Every..thing was a blur after th..at. I was outnumbered, and a Furiae Warrior came at me with…it's massive sword, and I..didn’t have time to react.”

Mydei winced. So that was how he got the wound. “After that?”

“Af-after that you arrived…and then I tri–tried to hide my wound and…tried to distract you, which, hah, didn’t…work.”

“Good thing you realized that.”

“And then you…noticed and got mad…and ri-ghtfully so. After that, my vision went…hazy. I tried to…listen to your voi..ce, but I was slipping…and fast. Then I felt…something under my back and…”

Phainon’s eyes widened a fraction. He reached for Mydei’s arm and grabbed his wrist. “You…you got me out of there, didn’t you? What I felt were…your arms.”

“Did you expect me to drag you by the foot?” Mydei scoffed. “And for the love of Nikador, next time you’re injured, can you say something about it? Hyacine said the healing process wasn’t easy with the amount of blood you lost. Do you…Do you have any idea how much you worried everyone out? You nearly died on this very bed. Have you no concern for your life?

Do you know how much you worried me out? was left unsaid.

Phainon looked a little hurt. His gaze drifted to their now intertwined fingers. “I’m sorry,” he whispered. “I didn’t mean to stress everyone out. I thought that…as the Deliverer I…I should be able to shrug the pain off.”

He laughed wetly and rubbed his eyes. “But that doesn’t ma...matter now. He smiled that smile again, the one reserved for Mydei and Mydei only, though it didn’t quite reach his ears. “You got me here in time. My hero.”

“You got extremely lucky,” said Mydei and sat down on the edge of the bed. He leaned in a little close and sighed softly. “Now, why do you have tears in your eyes, Phainon? There’s no reason to get emotional over this.”

“Hah! Says you,” said Phainon, sniffing and rubbing his eyes once more. “I’m not crying because of that. I’d never cry. I'm the Deliverer! I’d- hmph!"

The man was rudely cut off by Mydei, who decided to take matters in his own hands and wrapped his arms around the man and carefully pulled him into a hug. He heard Phainon inhale sharply and felt those small tears make their mark on his chiton. “It’s ok,” he said, closing his eyes and rubbing his back. “Today was a lot, wasn’t it? Too much for the two of us. It's ok to feel emotionally drained. We all feel like that once in a while now, don't we? Just rest, Phainon. I’ll be here.”

“Are you sure?” asked Phainon. "Because everyone makes promises, yet very few keep them."

“You really doubt me that much, you dumbass? I’m not one to break my promise now, aren’t I?”

Another laugh, this time a bit louder. “Yeah. Yeah, you never do break them.”

Mydei could text Hyacine later. For now, he continued to hold his friend and let him spill whatever grief he had in him. Once he was better, he swore he was going to make him promise to never hide anything like this ever again. From anyone or from him.

Marmoreal Market was nearly empty as the Curtain-Fall fell upon Okhema. Shop owners were closing their stores, and parents were calling for their children to come home. The light from the Dawn Device continued to shine, a constant reminder of Kephale’s sacrifice. A reminder of why the Flame-Chase must go on.

Mydei strolled through the streets, towards the Janus Device set up near the Forge. Usually, he’d either be sparring with the other Kremnoans from the detachment for a while or at the Chrysos Heir’s private baths with a tray of incense and some fruit. But certain… circumstances led to him traversing through the market and onto the roofs, where a certain white-haired swordsman was waiting for him. The crumpled note that started all this was shoved deep into his pocket.

It had been a week since the Titankin incident, and Phainon’s recovery was slow, but gradual. The medicines Hyacine prescribed were doing their jobs perfectly. The only issue he had was balancing himself on his feet (He nearly fell twice and would’ve had a broken nose or, at worst, a concussion if Mydei and Hyacine hadn’t caught him in time), but he’s been getting better. Yet, he hasn’t regained his full range of motion. The moron shouldn’t be out of bed, and here he was climbing buildings.

Then again, this was Phainon of all people. When has he ever listened to anyone?

The letter stated to meet him at the usual spot and, sure enough, he noticed that snowy white hair after crossing the canopy and jumped down to the balcony. Phainon had his arms crossed and eyes closed. If Mydei didn’t know any better, he would’ve thought the man was sleeping. He snorted under his breath.

“Hm? Already mocking me?” Phainon opened his eyes and tilted his head, smiling that smile again! Why does he do that all the time!? “I’m a wounded man, Mydeimos. Have some pity for me.”

“You want me to pity the person who’s not supposed to be here and instead resting in bed as his physician told him to do? Don’t expect any sympathy from me,” Mydei quipped, ignoring the fuzzy feeling blooming inside him. He moved to stand beside him. “Now spit it out, why did you want me to come here?”

Phainon laughed. “Relax! I just invited you to enjoy the scenery with me. Must you think I always have some ulterior motives whenever I call you for something?”

“Do you want me to write down a list?”

“...Ok so maybe sometimes I drag you along for a mission, but cut me some slack! I may be the strongest warrior in all of Okhema, but even I need some help from time to time.”

“The ‘strongest’ you say?” Mydei smirked. “Are you sure about that?”

“Hey! We’ve had many spars where it ended in a tie. If you don’t want me to claim the title, you can’t either.”

Phainon stuck his tongue out, and Mydei rolled his eyes. He lay down on the smooth surface and motioned for Phainon to do the same, which he happily did. Now they found themselves staring up at the clouds, the orange rays piercing through the sky. It wasn’t a ‘sunset’ by any means, but the light at this hour wasn’t so piercing. That was the miracle of the Dawn Device.

“It’s been a long time since I’ve ever seen a sunset.” Mydei voiced out, a bit surprised at his own words. Never has he ever said anything that made him sound so…weak? Vulnerable? Was admitting something so simple such as this meant a sign of weakness?

…No, he was being absurd. Kremnos had the usual day and night cycle before Nikador fell. The last time he truly saw the sunset was the night before his father dropped him into the Sea of Souls. He and his mother were sitting on the balcony. She was running her fingers through his hair while he asked her every question he had. She answered every single one of them with patience and love. Now that Mydei thought about it, her voice that day had sadness in it, and she was weaving her hand through his unruly hair very slowly. It seemed like she knew that his father was going to make that mad decision the next day…

Mydei shook his head. He couldn’t ask anyone the questions he had in his mind. Krateros was an option, but he knew that bringing up the topic of his mother would send him into a fit. He missed her, and so did Mydei. Some topics are too sensitive to bring up.

“I heard from the Kremnoan soldiers I spar with that the sunsets in Kremnos were beautiful. Is it true that the sky would always turn a beautiful shade of pink and orange with hints of purple dotted in various areas?”

“Most of the time, yes. There was a reason for that, but I don’t remember. There are some days when I’d find myself waiting for dusk to come. Of course, it never does.”

“The sun never sets in Okhema,” Phainon said, chuckling under his breath. “The light dims ever so slightly, but it’s never extinguished. I can relate to missing the sunset as well. Back at…at my home, my friends and I always rushed to the hill that overlooked the village to watch the stars slowly appear in the night sky. The moon follows after, gracing us with her presence and bathing us in her gentle, silvery glow.”

Mydei raised his brows. “Aedes Elysiae?” Phainon’s home that he never talked about?

“Yeah,” Phainon breathed out. “We would trace out the constellations and make up stories. Like the fishes forming a bond with the twins, or the centaur and the bull having a duel. There was no limit.”

“No wonder you have weird delusions about so many things.”

Phainon barked out a laugh. “Maybe.” His gaze lowered, and he met Mydei’s eyes. “I wonder, if you and I met when we were kids, do you think we would’ve been friends? I doubt I’d be able to drag you from the Palace, but from what you’ve said about your mother, I think she would’ve let you.”

“Honestly…maybe. But even then I’d be busy. Royal responsibilities and all.”

“Gah, that’s true. Royalty sucks sometimes, doesn’t it?”

“It’s not as bad as you think it is, Deliverer. And I have a question to ask.”

“Shoot.”

“This… is the first time you’ve ever talked about Aedes Elysiae. Why don’t you speak more about it?”

At that, Phainon looked a little sad. Like his question brought back some undesirable memories. “Because there’s nothing much to talk about. Aedes Elysiae was a small area. Insignificant in the eyes of history. You can’t compare it with the likes of Castrum Kremnos or Okhema, or even Aidonia. Everyone knows about Kremnos, and you're its Crowned Prince, of course, it makes sense for you to talk highly about your home. I’m just someone from a village no one will know about. ”

“...That doesn’t matter.” ‘That should never matter,’ Mydei thought. Even if Castrum Kremnos wasn’t the famed city it is with a long-lasting dynasty, he’d still talk about it with pride if given the chance. And he knows Phainon loves Aedes Elysiae with all his heart. His home shaped him, moulded him into the Hero he is today. “What matters are the memories that you made with your friends. Your family. Aedes Elysiae may not be famous, but it was still a place where people called home. The place that you called home.”

“I-”

“So don’t feel embarrassed and feel proud that you, Phainon, the Deliverer, and a Chrysos Heir on the path of the Flame-Chase are from a simple yet humble background with parents who would have loved you with all their being. No one will ever judge you. Heck, I definitely won’t, and I know you know that very well.”

“Mydei-”

“And I’m…actually kind of curious about your home. I only know about the great Deliverer, yet you know me and Castrum Kremnos. Isn’t that a little unfair?”

“You…are? I mean, you want to know?” Phainon asked. His voice was low, doubtful. Mydei could only wonder what thoughts were plaguing his mind. One of these days he’ll understand. For now, he wants the man to speak freely without any hesitation.

“Yes,” Mydei says firmly. He grabs Phainon’s hand and gently squeezes it. “I’m not lying when I earlier said that I’m genuinely curious about Aedes Elysiae. It sounds like you have a bunch of fond memories of the place.”

Phainon chuckled. “That I do. In that case… hmm…where do I even start?”

“Why not talk about your friends?”

“My friends, huh? Well, that certainly is a start.” Phainon took in a deep breath and exhaled slowly. His eyes were now looking up at the clouds. “I had a bunch of friends growing up. Despite my home being small, we were quite populated. Everyone got along with each other well and the kids always played in the grass or up the hill that overlooked the village. Sometimes we play hide-and-seek in the cornfields while the farmers watch us and laugh. They never minded as long as we didn’t damage any of the plants. Sometimes we like to weave flower crowns and play with wooden swords. I always manage to ‘stab’ everyone when I’m the king for the day, and they all complained it was because I had longer legs, so I ran faster than them.”

“No wonder you use a greatsword,” said Mydei, smirking. “You were training with one even before you were an adolescent.”

“I was inspired by the fairytales my mother read to me at night.”  Phainon shrugged. He shot a mischievous smile at him. “Now that I remember, we did have a small library that housed almost every fairytale ever written in Amphoreus, plus a few extra. It certainly wasn’t that impressive, but to us, every time we took a step inside, it felt like we were entering the Dream Land. I’m not sure if you’d like it though.”

“If there are books, that’s good enough for me.”

“I- really? So you…You know what, I’ll interrogate you about that later. Where was I again? Oh, yes ! Toy swords!”

Mydei snickered at the way Phainon’s hands moved as he continued to ramble on about the different games he played with his companions. He found it…endearing. He could see the tension slowly dissipating from him, replaced with pure, unadulterated happiness. He noticed how his eyes crinkled in the corners when talking about the games he played, his excited laughs when explaining what he called the ‘best parts’ made his heart warm up a little. Phainon was a happy and outgoing person in general, but this was the first time Mydei had seen him glowing.

Hopefully, once everything is said and done and the Flame-Chase is over, Phainon would no longer need to hide behind a mask.

“Out of all my friends,” Phainon said, and Mydei felt him squeeze his hand again, “there was one who stood out the most.” His voice was low, mourning. “She and I met under some… very unique circumstances, but she was the first friend I ever made. I…think you would’ve liked her. I can see you and her getting along splendidly.”

“What was her name?”

“Cyrene.”

‘Cyrene.’ “That’s a lovely name,” said Mydei.

“She was a lovely person,” said Phainon. “We’d go chase the fairies in the afternoon after we’d finish eating our lunch. Sometimes we’d have a picnic under the singular tree on the hill. She’d always make me flower crowns and bracelets and tell me all sorts of stories she heard from other people. She was someone who was shrouded in mystery, but she was the kindest person I ever met- and that’s saying a lot, considering everyone in the village were really nice people. Oh, and growing up I used to have terrible nightmares. Like, terrible ones where I’d wake up screaming my lungs out. My parents tried everything they could to get them to stop, but nothing worked. I told Cyrene about it, and she volunteered to stop by my house every night at around 10:00 to sing me a lullaby. At first, I doubted it’d work. My mother tried to do just that, and it did put me to sleep just fine, but an hour later I was wide awake with sweat covering my forehead. Yet, I let her try and, to my absolute shock and surprise, I woke up the next morning completely well rested with not even a single nightmare. I told her excitedly that it worked, and she laughed and elbowed me in the ribs, telling me it’d work. We had a long laugh before she started making another flower crown.”

Mydei hummed, picturing a young Phainon playing in the grass with a wide smile, being chased by a girl with lemonade-pink hair, giggling loudly and making flower crowns under a tree. Having a friend like that…he knows someone like her is having a built-in support system that someone could always rely on. And from what he’s said, Phainon and Cyrene were each other’s support system. He had friends that he always hung out with in the library or the training grounds, but he never got to experience the thrill of childhood. It was always him and his mother.

He squeezed Phainon’s hand to get his attention. “You know, if she were still…I’d love to meet her.”

Phainon’s eyes were watering a little again, but that soft smile stayed. "Heh, just like I said."

"Just like you said."

Phainon let go of his hand and shifted closer, resting his head on Mydei's arm with a contented sigh, showing no remorse for his attempt to cut off his blood circulation. If he had done this in the beginning when they met, Mydei would've just shoved him off. The little weasel thinks he has him wrapped up in his little metaphorical finger?

...His hands were stroking his scalp. Tenderly too, if he may add. Welp, it is indeed the end of the universe. The proud Prince of Castrum Kremnos was now a sappy idiot.

But, with Phainon, he'll let himself loosen up a little. At least there was no one watching them.

Chapter End Notes

Chapter Notes

This is short chapter but I'm releasing this chapter a little earlier because I think the last chapter (we're already on the last chapter?? The art of gift-giving. If it could be called an art.

There’s no specific occasion where one needs to give something to their loved ones. In fact, it happens almost all the time in the Holy City. Of course, there was Mnestia’s Day, where almost all the gift shops would be crowded with spouses picking out the perfect last-minute gifts for their lovers or family members. Love wasn’t restricted to only romance after all.

But this particular gift that Mydei had in mind was one he commissioned about a week ago to Chartonus, and today just so happened to be the day he had to go to collect it.

Phainon was not currently in Okhema, having been deployed to Janusopolis to help some of the priests fend off the abominations of the Black Tide while they perform some prayer. He wasn’t sure of the details, but Lady Tribbie was with him to smoothen out any possible complications. Their numbers weren’t huge, so Aglaea sent only him to deal with it.

“It shouldn’t take long,” he had said when they were at the bakery trying out the new pastries the day before the mission. He gently bumped his shoulder. “I'll be in and out of there before you know it, and then we’ll return to our daily sparring session.”

“Try not to get injured and then we’ll see,” Mydei scoffed, flicking his forehead. Phainon let out an indignant yelp and kicked his shin. “Kephale knows what you’ll do to yourself this time, just like last time where-”

“Ok, do we need to talk about last time?” said Phainon, glaring at him. “I said I would never repeat that. Have some faith in me, Mydei!”

“If only,” Mydei muttered under his breath. Phainon huffed.

“But I will be fine. Besides, I’ll be with Lady Tribbie. If anything happens to me, I swear I’ll tell her. It’s not like I cannot hide any wounds from her…”

That…was true. The triplets may look like children, but everyone knows they are the wisest individuals among both the people of Amphoreus and the Chrysos Heirs. Oh, and nothing escapes their sights. Especially when it comes to Lady Tribbie. Perhaps that’s the reason why Aglaea wanted her to tag along. Well, good on her part. The Deliverer needed a babysitter.

Mydei took a bite out of his honey cake and cleared his throat. “If anything happens and you hide it from me, I will ask Lady Tribbie for all the details. Do you understand me?”

“Aye aye, captain!” Phainon exclaimed, throwing him a mock salute. Mydei rolled his eyes and shoved a piece of cake in the other’s mouth to shut him up, and smirked when he started to cough and wheeze. He slid his cup of water over the table and roared with laughter when Phainon all but yoinked the chalice and gulped everything down in one go. Oh, how he wished he had his teleslate with him.

It didn't take him long to reach Chartonus’ shop, where he found the Mountain-Dweller hammering away on the forge. There were no signs of his assistants, which struck him as odd, but he figured they might be doing something else. He waved to the blacksmith when he managed to catch his eye. “Chartonus!”

“Prince Mydeimos,” said Chartonus, setting aside his hammer to grab something from his table. “Came on time, you did. Your order finished, I did yesterday.”

“Thank you. Where are Tum and Siskel?”

“A task, I sent them to do. Before Action Hour tomorrow, they will arrive. Inspect your weapon, for now.”

Chartonus set the sword and bow down on the bench for Mydei to inspect. He carefully picked the blade up and looked at it from all angles. The designs were a bit complicated, which was why Mydei had commissioned him one week in advance with a drawing of how he wanted it to look.

Now, he knows Phainon’s greatsword was virtually unbreakable, having been forged by Chartonus himself, but it’s always good to have a wide array of weaponry in one's arsenal. As for the bow, well, Phainon has been getting quite better at his aim recently, and Mydei was beyond impressed when he shot three arrows at once right and landed them all at the center of the target. He knew he was ready to try using a better-built bow. More specifically, a recurve bow.

Mydei wanted them to look the same but also a little different. The body of the bow was primarily silver with blue accents and three blue feathers on both the upper and lower tips. Little half sun motifs were on each tiller with a sturdy grip right in the middle. He tested the string on the bow, humming in satisfaction at the smooth draw. It wasn’t too tight either. The sword, on the other hand, was what he was the most excited about.

While the bow was a bright silver glimmering in the night, the sword was obsidian black with a crescent moon at the hilt with a circular frame. The blade was long and sharp, slightly bent at the top to help kill enemies faster. He gently bent the sword’s tip and performed a few slow swings. Everything looked perfect.

“Thank you, Chartonus,” Mydei said with a small smile, giving the weapons back to the blacksmith so he could wrap them up. "They look and feel wonderful, especially considering I only gave you one week. I should have said this before, but my apologies for asking you to make these on such short notice.”

“No need to apologize, there is,” said Chartonus, waving him off with his hand. "Create anything you want in one week, I can. Always honored to craft weapons for the Chrysos Heirs, I am.”

Of course he was. Chartonus has always been proud to aid in the Flame Chase journey in his own way. Sometimes he’d stop to wonder just what his ancestors were thinking when they decided to enslave the Mountain-Dwellers. Mydei had great respect for Chartonus for breaking the shackles of his people and setting them free. He wasn’t privy to all the details, but he struck a deal with one of the Kremnoan High Elders that he’d do…something in exchange for his people’s freedom.

Quite frankly, he didn’t want to know.

After paying for the weapons (he unceremoniously dropped the coin sack before speed walking out of there lest Chartonus finds out he paid double the intended amount and chase after him), he made his way to the Heir’s private quarters. He knows for a fact that Phainon rarely ever keeps his room locked because the man admitted it to him on a random day. His reason was that they never had locks to their doors and no one ever stole from them. Regardless, Mydei still gently scolded him and told him to always be wary of his surroundings even outside the battlefield. They both know some people wanted to eliminate them. The Council of Elders certainly wanted to recall the power they gave to the Heir’s as soon as possible and eliminate them.

…To his credit, the Deliverer was trying his best to change his habits, but there were some days when he’d forget and leave his room completely forgetting to slide the lock into place. Like today. However, just this once, Mydei was happy he did.

He opened the door and went straight to his drawer, setting the package on his bed along the way. Mydei grabbed a piece of parchment, one of Phainon’s quills, a bottle of ink, and started to write out a letter.

Deliverer

I’m not sure when you’ll be back, but something tells me you’ll be here tomorrow. I won’t be up to greet you and Lady Tribbie, so I’m leaving these here for you. Inside the package, you’ll find two weapons handcrafted by Chartonus himself, so don’t worry about their quality.

You’ve gotten better with handling a bow recently, so I thought it was about time you had a proper one. As for the sword, you can’t always rely on that one greatsword of yours. Better have some backup weapons in case you lose your greatsword to your carelessness, which I can see happening.

Anyways, we’ll test them out when we spar the next day. There’s no need to thank me for this, so it will be unnecessary to send me a text back. I do hope you enjoy these little offerings.

-Mydei

Mydei screwed the ink bottle shut, placed both it and the quill back in their proper places and kept the letter on top of the package. Then, without looking back, he headed for his own room, but not before locking the door from the outside. Of course, that isn’t going to do much, but don’t they say it’s the thought that counts?

The rays from the Dawn Device crept through the curtains as the Entry Hour greeted the Holy City. The streets are slowly filling with residents as they set up their shops and restock their wares.

Mydei sat up on his bed and rubbed his eyes, blinking away the last vestiges of sleep that clung to him. Today was going to be a long day-training some of the youngsters from the Kremnoan Detachment, helping advertise the new honey cakes the bakery made, as well as getting some free samples once it’s over), supervise a race for the kids (because why not?) and train a bit by himself. He couldn’t remember the last time his schedule was this packed.

He stretched his arms for a bit and, without looking, grabbed his teleslate when his fingers brushed against something smooth and slightly waxy. He looked up to find, lo and behold, a rolled-up piece of parchment sitting next to his teleslate, held together by a white string. He didn’t have to think long to know who had placed it there.

Of course, Phainon would want to thank him somehow, despite telling him it wasn’t needed. But then again…

‘...Cute.’

Since he made such an effort to write a thank you, Mydei couldn’t just throw it away without reading first. Feeling a smirk tugging at his lips, he untied the string and let the parchment unfurl.

Mydei

First off, you know I’d write a letter back to you to say thanks-I mean, I could’ve just said thank you in person, but we all know how busy the Crown Prince is these days. Second, you can’t exactly be mad at me for writing a letter back when you clearly mentioned I shouldn’t text you.

As for the gifts, I feel honored. When did you have the time to go behind my back and commission all these? I think I need to interrogate Chartonus to know your secrets! But alas, I decided against it. The bow feels pretty light, and its draw power is super strong. It feels ten times better than the training one. And as for the sword, well, you’ve finally given me the key to finishing my Dark Swordsmaster get-up. Hahaha, nothing is stopping me now! Not even Aglaea! Now the whole world will soon know about their shining hero in black!

I know you’re busy the whole morning and afternoon, so let's have a spar at around 6:00. That is, if you think you can still stand on your own two feet by then. Kephale knows you need strength. But anyway, I will see you later!

-Phainon

“...HKS,” Mydei muttered, rolling his eyes. A fond smile replaced the smirk on his face. He could imagine that dork’s smile as he wrote the letter, the smile that made him weak most of the time. He chuckled and kept the letter on the table and his way to his closet to start getting ready for the day. But, as he was choosing what to wear for the day, a thought occurred to him…

Wait a second…

How did Phainon manage to break into his room and place the letter on his bedside table? And then he realized he forgot to read the note at the bottom of the letter.

Mydei ran back to the table and unscrolled the parchment.

P:S: You left your room unlocked. Starting to develop my bad habits I see.

He slammed his head on the wall.

Chapter End Notes
