The wind was gentle, stirring up small flecks of dirt from the ground. Specks of something black were scattered in various places, which Mydei instantly recognized as ashes. It’s so ironic that the place reeked of death, yet the grass continued to grow, leeching off the remains of the dead.

From where they were standing, Mydei could see everything, and nothing. If he closed his eyes, he could envision how the village looked at its prime. The rice and cornfields swaying in the breeze, the loud laughter of the children, the hustle and bustle of the people. He could only wonder what Phainon must be thinking at the moment.

Never in a million years did Mydei imagine he would find himself standing on the hill Phainon had told him countless stories about. The hill he and his friends laid on to watch the stars, where they had picnics. The hill that overlooked his home.

Aedes Elysiae.

Or whatever was left of it.

He remembered Phainon’s words- the crimson moon that hung over the sky as the Black Tide swept everything away. That black-robed swordmaster who slayed Cyrene, the cries of the people. As the Demi-God of Strife, he had now gained a new understanding—not only of war and bloodlust in battle but also of its aftermath: the fear, the loss, and the pain. Divinity wiped away Aglaea’s emotions, but for Mydei, it only heightened them.

Mydei closed his eyes again and sighed in relief when he couldn’t sense any monsters. The last thing they needed was Titankin to ruin the moment. He didn’t want to stain any part of the land with his blood crystals. Beside him, Phainon looked…uneasy, for the most part. There was an unreadable expression on his face. If he remembered correctly, it’s the Deliverer’s first time returning home since the incident.

"Phainon?" Mydei said, concern seeping into his voice. He hadn’t spoken a word during their trip, which unsettled him. At first, it made sense—anyone would fall silent when returning to the ruins of the place they once called home. But this felt different, too different. He’d expected him to comment here and there, but not even a single peep came out of his mouth. Another ability he acquired after claiming the Core Flame was sensing the emotions seeping from others. It allowed him to detect his enemies from afar and gave him time to prepare his attack. Right now, it was making him a bit uneasy.

As he expected, he got no response. “Phainon,” Mydei tried again, bumping his shoulder into his. Phainon let out a tiny gasp and snapped his head up, muscles all tensed. He raised a brow and crossed his arms. “Are you ok?”

“Never better!” he exclaimed, putting on what Mydei immediately identified as a ‘phony grin,’ and Mydei narrowed his eyes. Phainon chuckled nervously under his scrutinizing glare and rubbed the back of his neck, that grin instantly melting off his face. “Ok, yeah, I’m not feeling well. In fact, I think I feel sick.”

That wasn’t surprising. It wasn’t only the stench of death that made them nauseous. The whole place looked like a warzone.

“This isn’t how I wanted you to see my home,” he heard Phainon say. His head hung low again, his bangs covering his face. “I thought…I was under the impression something must have survived here. A house, or maybe a door. But from here…I don’t see anything.”

“You never saw the village after the incident?”

“I turned around and never looked back. Like a coward.” Phainon hissed.

“Stop it,” Mydei said, smacking his shoulder. “Even if you had, there’s nothing you could have done. You were young and powerless. You were just a child.”

“If only I hadn’t been one," that familiar, broken whisper escaped him. A tone Phainon rarely used—but when he did, it was to tear himself down. To blame himself for things beyond his control, yet things he believed would have ended differently if only he had been stronger. It hurt everyone to see him get emotional over this. His thoughts, his dreams, his nightmares all stem from one place and one place alone.

And…in some ways, he could relate to the feeling. His mother sacrificed herself so that he could keep living. Thanks to Caelus’ time–travelling abilities and the power to access memory fragments, he found out his accursed father had been poisoning her daily, leading up to that ill–fated battle. The rage he felt that day was so strong, he almost demanded Caelus that he’d be sent back in time just so he could kill that wretched, pathetic excuse of a human being all over again. His blood crystals were growing out of his body in response to the overwhelming fury, and it was only after Caelus shook him hard by the shoulders and yelled at him to snap out of it that he finally managed to calm down, though the crystals took a while to disappear.

Case in point, they both had regrets. Many regrets, but there wasn’t anything they could do about it now. All they could do is keep pushing forward towards that promised new tomorrow. That was the only way the dead could truly be avenged. They both knew that. Today was the day Phainon was going to face his past after so many years.

“Are you ready to go down there?”

“I…”

"Or we could wait a few minutes until you’ve pulled yourself together."

“No,” Phainon said with such conviction it made Mydei hesitate a little. But before he could say anything, the Deliverer continued to speak. “If I keep second-guessing myself I’ll never go down there and face my fears. I’m ready, Mydei. I am.”

Mydei sighed and shook his head, a small smile adorning his face. Oh, that Deliverer. He’d never change, and that was probably for the better. “In that case, lead the way.”

“Of course, my Prince. Just try to keep up.”

“The demigod of Strife doesn’t need someone to tell him to ‘keep up.’”

“Sure sure. Next time I see you trudging far behind me, I’ll assume it’s for dramatic effects. The blood crystals add a nice touch too.”

Phainon cackled as Mydei hurled a string of Kremnoan curses at him.

Mydei felt like someone was twisting a knife into his gut as he walked through the fields. Phainon was ahead of him, walking at a much slower pace, no doubt taking it all in. Ashes were in the air, on the ground, and he couldn’t tell which of them were from wood and which were from the…from the long gone corpses.

He could feel the lingering touch of Thanatos weighing heavily on his back. His now sharp and clear eyesight could make out faint bloodstains that had not faded with time. When Castrum Kremnos fell, there was at least something in the city he could salvage from the ruins for the other soldiers. Nothing here survived. Not even a single piece of plank.

Phainon twirled around, the sun casting a warm glow on his hair, beckoning him to come stand next to him. “This, if memory serves me right, is where my house used to be.”

Mydei could make out the outline of where the house stood. A bit big, probably bigger than most of the other houses here. If Caelus and Mem had tagged along, they could have used Oronyx’s blessing to see the village before it was destroyed, but he doubted that was something Phainon would want to see now. He mentioned the houses were built using tar and bricks, and the doors from a large oak tree. As expected, there wasn’t anything here, not even bones.

The Flame Reaver made sure nothing was left behind.

“I remember the story of how the house was built,” Phainon said, and his voice was starting to crack a little. He brushed his hand against his, and he grabbed it with no hesitation. “My mother and father met at this very spot under the moon when they were teenagers. I wouldn’t call it love at first sight, but from what my mom told me, it might as well have been. Dad made her a flower crown and she got all flustered. She said, “What kind of man walks up to a random woman he’s never met, gives her a flower crown, and acts all flirtatious with her?” in the most comical, exaggerated voice ever.”

Mydei snorted. That explained why Phainon was a romantic at heart. “I’m assuming it worked then.”

“It worked well. More than well. Soon after, they found themselves meeting here often with little gifts in hand. They weren’t anything grand by all means, but they meant the world to them. Then, one day, my dad brought a brick and a box. It turned out that he was preparing to propose to her and lay down that brick as a sort of foundation to start their new relationship. My mom said yes, and the rest is history. They happily got married at the center of the village under a beautiful flower arch. She said it was the most beautiful day of her life—along with the day I was born.”

“So, the magnificent Deliverer really did come into this world screaming his tiny head off.”

“Pfft, Mydei!” Phainon exclaimed, shoving the prince while said prince howled in laughter. “All babies come into the world screaming. Also, my head is not tiny! Also, what a way to ruin the damp mood, Mr. Demi-God of Strife.”

"You laughed too,” Mydei snorted, rapping him on the top of his head. He snickered when he heard the man yelp. “If I hadn’t said anything sooner you’d be brooding right about now, and it’d be harder for me to snap you out of it.” It was the truth. He honestly loved that Phainon was telling him more stories of his childhood, but right now he looked like he needed an emotional break. Besides, teasing him now and then was his forte. He was glad divinity hadn’t stripped him of that.

Phainon pouted, puffing up his cheek. He placed one hand on his hip and pointed an accusatory finger at him. “I don’t brood, Mydeimos. Brooding is not my thing. I don’t know how to brood. You, on the other hand, brooded all the time when you were in Okhema. So much so, I have to drag you from all your hiding spots all the time to get you to spar with me, and that somehow always works!”

“Because it just so happened that a spar was exactly what I needed to cheer myself up all the time. Have you considered that as a possibility?” Mydei shot back, smirking.

“Right. A spar was exactly what you needed to cheer yourself up all the time. Sure thing, Mydei, sure.”

Phainon faced the ruins, and his next words came out softer. “Thanks for the small distraction. I really appreciate it but…I kind of need to be alone right now here.” He let out a bitter laugh. “I-I know I may sound rude and everything but I need thi-”

“Shut up-again,” Mydei cut him off, squeezing his shoulder. “Why are you apologizing? I get it, and I’m certainly not offended. If you need some space, just say so. I’ll be here if you need me, ok?”

“Thank you,” Phainon muttered. With that, Mydei stepped away and decided to explore a little. He made sure to maintain his distance but to stay as close as he could in case Phainon called him. The idiot. One of these days, he’ll come visit Okhema just to beat some sense into the man.

The sun was hanging below the sky, and the wind was starting to pick up. Mydei brushed his bangs from his face and knelt. Hovering his hand over the ash-covered ground, he closed his eyes, reaching out to the land as it once was, searching for anything that remained. Back in Castrum Kremnos, he saw the city as it had been at its peak—soldiers lined up on the stairs, and people from the past celebrating their king’s long-awaited return. It was sort of similar to Caelus’ ability, but he couldn’t access memory fragments or bring the past to life. However, he does use it sometimes to replay some moments, gaining information as to what went on during his time in the Sea of Souls and leading up to his father's death.

He became something of a history nerd after that. Looking at the past gave him more information than he could ever dream of. None of what he saw would be in the books in his library, or any other library for that matter. It was as his mother said-only the strong will note what happened. Only the ones with power would. The truth may never be fully uncovered unless someone actually tries to look for it. Now, speaking of the library…

Mydei jogged down a stone path and found what he was looking for-the remains of a leather book. The very tattered remains of a leather book.

So this was where the library stood. It wasn’t huge by any means, but it appeared it was big enough to house all the books the people here would ever need.

He ran his fingers against the material, letting the story speak for itself. It was a diary that belonged to a young girl. A thick one that had many pages and held many tales. He couldn’t make out the full details of how the girl looked, though he managed to catch a few glimpses-cerulean eyes with pink dots scattered around the iris, shoulder-length lemon-pink hair framing her face with a small white clip pinned on the right. A dark purple and white dress with long sleeves…why did this sound familiar to him?”

Mydei stood up and continued to walk down the faded path, his heart pounding in his chest. The leaves from the trees fell from the branches, some landing on his hair and body. A mixture of gold and green, crunching under his foot. He tried to recall where he had seen someone like that. Has he seen someone like that before?

So far, he found nothing of value. He had hoped to find something to salvage here, but considering the intensity of the fire, coupled with the Black Tide, finding anything intact would be nothing short of a miracle. Mydei’s eyes scanned the area, hoping to find something that might help him uncover more memories. Maybe then, he’ll know what happened to the village in the aftermath of the fire and tell Phainon. Maybe some survivors managed to escape in time and are taking refuge somewhere. If that’s the case, they could bring them back to Okhema. That is, if there were any, and from what Phainon told him, his hopes were low.

So far, nothing. He wondered what the Deliverer was doing right about now. It was about time he checked on her.

As he was about to turn away and check somewhere else and Phainon, a sudden gleam of white caught his attention from the corner of his eye. Squinting, he broke into a jog toward the bushes where the light was coming from and brushed them aside.

Right there, caught on one of the twigs, he found the source. It looked to be an exquisite hairpin. It had a golden diamond with small scorch marks and two torn petals on either side. It was a simple thing, yet also really beautiful.

Holding his breath, Mydei carefully extracted the pin from the bush and made sure his talons didn't accidentally damage the accessory any further. It stayed intact in his hands, and he let out a breath he hadn’t realized he was holding. He found something. He actually found something .

Making his way back to the place where the library was, he closed his eyes. Mydei couldn’t make out anything at first-all there was only darkness, until he heard laughter. A girl’s laughter echoed around him. She sounded young, maybe around fifteen or sixteen years old. Then he saw flashes of pink hair, followed by a purple and white dress with gold accents. Once again, deja vu hit him like a Dromas charging at him at full speed, and he couldn't figure out for the life of him why.

Whatever. He'll figure it out later. For now, he should go show Phainon what he found.

And so he tucked the clip into his little pouch and made his way back up the little slope where Phainon was standing. His cape was flitting in the wind, his posture rigid. He saw the man opening and clenching his fists. He looked like he was about to burst a vein. Typical Deliverer, needing someone to bring him back to solid ground.

Mydei shoved him.

Phainon screamed.

He laughed hard.

Phainon scowled at him. “What was that for!?”

“Nothing,” Mydei replied, wheezing. He straightened up and coughed. “But in all seriousness, it’s ok to mourn, but if I hadn’t done that, you’d be trapped somewhere in your pretty little brain and never come back. Remember to not lose yourself.”

He sighed and walked into Mydei’s open arms. “I know,” he sighed, hugging him back. “I guess I’m glad to have you here.”

"You should be.”

“But why are you here? Weren’t you looking for things to read?”

“First of all, it’s not called reading, Deliverer. And second, I’m here because…I found something I need to show you.”

“WHAT?” Phainon looked up, eyes blown wide. His grip around Mydei tightened. “Mydei, what are you talking about? You mean to say you…actually found something?”

Mydei nodded. “I know it sounds absurd, but I have the object in my pouch. It’s a little scorched, but otherwise intact."

Phainon’s breathing hitched. His hands trembled as he pulled away from the prince. Staggering back on shaky legs, he rasped, “I don’t believe it.” Even his voice sounded raw. Mydei took a step forward, his gauntleted hand reaching out, but Phainon only backed away further. “I-I can’t for some reason. That fire didn’t leave behind even a single straw of hay. And yet you found something whole?”

And all of a sudden he started to laugh hysterically, throwing one arm across his face. “I can’t believe this. I just can’t believe it! Whatever you found back there, it can’t be real. Check your pouch again. It must be dust by now.”

Mydei gritted his teeth, unsure of what to say. Phainon’s laughter ceased, and his gaze was now elsewhere, biting his lower lip. In the dying light, he could see the tears gathering in his eyes. It was… weird seeing him so beaten down. And depressing. He looked so…so young and helpless right now, it pained him.

He reached into his pouch and grabbed the clip, smiling to himself– it was still intact. However, the weird sense of deja vu hit him hard once again upon laying his fingers on it. It was as if his body-his senses to be more specific, were screaming at him that they knew who the owner of the clip was.

“Phainon,” he called out. “Come here. I think you’ll be surprised that my little finding has, in fact, not turned into dust as you had put it.”

Phainon hesitated, eyes flickering at him and where he was standing. He looked torn between coming closer or staying put, like a frightened animal. No matter.

He’ll just go up to him and show him. No words, no grand gestures-just walk up and show him that what was in his hand was real.

So, he did just that. He stood right in front of Phainon, gently placed two fingers under his chin, and lifted his head. Then he let go and held up the pin. From this angle, the gold of the clip caught the light perfectly, casting it in an elegant, radiant glow. Mydei had to admit whoever made it had some remarkable skill.

However, instead of smiling or feeling happy, Phainon’s eyes widened in fear and something else, his body stiffening like he had just seen a ghost. His body started to tremble violently again, and he backed away. Mydei tilted his head in confusion, lowering his hand. That… wasn’t what he was expecting. Shock, yes. Bewilderment? Obviously. But fear?

“Phainon?”

“Where did you get that?” Phainon asked, his voice cracking. His gaze stayed locked on the pin resting in Mydei’s hand. Slowly, he curled in on himself, as if trying to disappear. Mydei’s confusion deepened — this wasn’t the reaction he had expected at all.

He took a step forward. “Phainon? What’s going-”

“Answer the damn question, Mydei!” Phainon yelled. He was getting more frazzled by the second. “Where the fuck did you find that? The exact spot! ”

“On the branch of a bush!” he answered quickly. “Like I said before, it was near the library. What’s going on, Phainon? Talk to me!”

But Phainon never did. Instead, he stumbled back, slapping a hand over his mouth as he screamed a string of desperate no’s. Tears streamed down his face as sobs began to rack his body. Mydei screamed his name, but he didn’t respond. A wave of fear crashed over him.

What was going on? What was happening? Was there something he was missing? Was there…

Wait.

His visions…that girl–

Oh.

It hit him. Judging by Phainon’s reaction, the clip wasn’t just important — it was significant . But it wasn’t about the clip itself. It was about the one who owned it. A girl with lemon-pink hair and bright blue eyes. A girl who used to run through the fields in a white and purple dress. A girl Phainon cherished more than anything, deep in his heart.

Oh.

Oh Titans.

Did he just make a mistake?

Phainon had thought when he and Mydei first arrived at the ruins of Aedes Elysiae that there would be nothing left to find. After all, the massive fire had burned everything to ash. Not even the skeletal remains of the people had survived. The Flame Reaver had made sure there were no survivors- and that nothing remained.

And yet, Mydei was here, holding Cyrene’s hairpin. Cyrene’s hairpin. He remembered watching that wretched, vile swordmaster cut her down right in front of his eyes. He saw the light leave her eyes. She died in his arms with a small smile on her face. He gripped her hand tightly, afraid to let her go. He couldn’t let her go. Tears had started to fall uncontrollably from his eyes, and his throat hurt with all the screaming he had done. What almost made him laugh was that Cyrene was trying to comfort him. Comfort him! Whilst she was dying! Phainon was so close to telling her to shut up and conserve her energy.

He knew saying that was hopeless, but he did anyway. And when she faded to dust, everything was gone. No trace of Cyrene remained. Nothing was there. So how does that explain the pin in his hand?

“No. No no no no no no no ! ” Phainon said, covering his mouth, choking back tears. It couldn’t be. It couldn’t be. This has got to be some nasty prank, right? Mydei was pulling a prank on him to make him laugh! That’s got to be it, yes!

But…Mydei wasn’t that kind of person. He understands Phainon more than anyone else. He knew what pain and loss felt like, and he wouldn’t wish that on anyone. The sadness on his face only confirmed it—this was real. At that moment, he found himself wondering if Cyrene had worn her hair clip when she died. And even then, the fire and the Black Tide left nothing intact.

He forced his mouth to work, but all that came out were broken words. “Please tell me my eyes aren’t working, Mydei. Please tell me that isn’t real. It can’t be.”

Through his blurry vision, he saw Mydei approaching slowly, one hand gently outstretched. He said something, but Phainon didn’t hear him. His heart thundered, and it felt as if a hand had wrapped around his lungs, tightening with every breath he took. His entire body was shaking as memories-those damn memories that he shoved into the dark recesses of his mind were now flooding his mind, drowning him. ‘Oh Titans, I think I’m actually going to die.’

He furiously rubbed his eyes in an attempt to clear his vision to no avail. His heart and body started to hurt terribly. Despite all his efforts a tiny sob tore escaped his mouth. Then another one. Then another, until they started to rattle his whole body and he started to hyperventilate. He heard Mydei yell out his name. He wanted to respond, but every nerve in his body was on fire.

Whatever strength he had left his body, and Phainon collapsed to his knees. Pain flared through them, but he hardly noticed. Instead, he clutched himself and sobbed, yelling Cyrene’s name like it might bring her back, every breath wracked with grief. And it was all because of one small hair clip—a simple thing, yet it carried a story all its own.

“Cyrene!” Phainon yelled, waving his arms. “There you are!”

“Hm? Where else would I be silly?” said Cyrene in a playful tone, flicking his forehead. He jumped back and groaned, rubbing the area gently.

“Well, I thought you would be at your home at this time, but you weren’t there. And I couldn’t find you anywhere in the village.”

“And so you came to the one spot you knew I’d be in.”

“You say I’m easy to read, but you are too, Cyrene.”

“Has anyone ever told you that you’re so cute?” Cyrene said, reaching over to pinch Phainon’s cheeks. He dodged them effortlessly and moved to sit down on the other side, glaring at her. She laughed. “Fine, I’ll let your cheeks survive for one day.”

Phainon huffed and muttered, “Why not on all the days?” Cyrene merely rolled her eyes. “Anyways, stop distracting me! Let me talk now!”

“Alright, alright. So then, why has our heroic Deliverer sought out this pretty damsel today?”

“No reason, I just wanted to give you something,” Phainon said, fishing something out of his back pocket. He didn’t miss the way her eyes twinkled in surprise. “I had some help from my mother, but I wanted to make something as a thank you present for being my friend. ”

Silly little goose, why are you thanking me for being your friend?” Cyrene laughed, reaching out to ruffle his hair, earning a squawk from Phainon. “No matter what, we’ll always be friends. You really didn’t have to make anything for me.”

“First of all, shut up,” Phainon said, putting a finger on her lips. He narrowed his eyes. “I wanted to make something for you, so you have no choice but to accept. Now, close your eyes and give me your hand. And do not open them unless I tell you to.”

“Oh? Should I be worried?” Cyrene teased, arching a brow but closing her eyes anyway, a mischievous smile tugging at her lips. Phainon groaned once again and muttered, “You are way too dramatic for your own good.” He grabbed her hand and placed his gift on her palm, and closed it. He then placed her hand on her chest. She giggled again. “Am I supposed to be feeling something, Phainon?”

“No! It’s just a small gesture. Now, open your eyes and see what I’ve given you.”

He smirked when she saw him slowly open her hand and chuckled under his breath when her eyes widened. In her palm was a hair clip. A simple yet beautiful thing. A gold diamond with two white petals made of soft fabric pinned at the top, fluttering in the wind. He made the petals and painstakingly carved out the diamond and asked his mother to stitch them together. He was very proud of the result.

And seeing Cyrene’s surprised look made him feel even prouder.

“You,” she started to say, opening and closing her mouth. Her blue eyes met his own. “Phainon, this looks so pretty! I can’t believe you made this all on your own. How long did you spend working on this?”

“About a week,” Phainon replied. “It took some time to get the shape of the petals right. I thought I was about to run out of fabric by the time I was done. The pin was actually the easiest to make. Well, ok, I didn’t make it. I took it from my mother's box of charms, but enough of my rambling, what do you think?”

Phainon waited for her response, hesitating when she didn’t say anything. Panic started to set in. Did she like it? She said it was beautiful. What if she just said that to make him happy? Was this a good idea? He didn’t make her unhappy, did he?

Before he started to spiral and jump down into yet another rabbit hole, Cyrene pulled him into a hug, the clip still in her hand. Phainon tried to raise his head, but he found he couldn’t do so. “Er, Cyrene…?”

“I can hear your thoughts from here,” Cyrene hummed, hugging him tighter. “You are quite the overthinker, aren’t you, my dear Deliverer?”

“I was hoping you’d say something,” Phainon muttered. “I thought you didn’t like it.”

“Relax! I love it. It was…it was very thoughtful of you. I’ll wear it every day.”

“Ok, you don’t have to do that! ”

“Well, I want to,” said Cyrene, pulling them apart. Her right hand was resting on his shoulder.

She flicked her eyes toward the pin, wordlessly gesturing to him. “Now, if I’m to keep up my promise, I’m going to need some help pinning it to my hair.”

She wiggled her eyebrows, and for a second Phainon stared at her, dumbfounded. His eyes were probably blown wide before he processed what she said and burst in laughter.

Cyrene raised a brow, mock-glaring at him, though she was starting to laugh too. “What’s so funny?”

“No-nothing,” Phainon gasped, shaking his head. He took a few breaths and said in a more even tone, “Nothing, Cyrene. Now turn around so I can put this in your hair.”

“Alright,” she said, tilting her head. Phainon grabbed the pin from her and grabbed a few strands of her hair. Cyrene started to hum a tune under her breath, drumming her fingers on her lap. He stuck his tongue out and once he managed to slide the pin into place and made sure it was secure, he let go.

“All done.” Phainon pulled out a mirror. “How does it look?”

Cyrene grabbed the mirror, inspected herself for a few seconds, kept it aside, and pulled him into another hug. Phainon bit his tongue to hold back a scream. “It’s beautiful,” she whispered. “I promise I’ll always wear this until I am called to the Sea of Souls.”

“Woah, uhm,” Phainon sputtered, pulling back, feeling his cheeks heating up, “I appreciate that you like it and all, but it’s like I said before-you don’t have to wear it every day.”

“But I want to,” said Cyrene. “You spent days working on it. It’d be most disrespectful if I don’t wear it. And thank you, Phainon. Thank you so much.”

“Heh, you’re welcome.”

“Now then, why don’t you say we go chase some fairies and enact some scenes from a book I borrowed yesterday from the library? We’ll call the others too.”

“Yes!”

The two children giggled, not knowing that that was going to be the last day they’d ever be together. The last day of peace, before the sun turned red and darkness swept the land.

“Oh, Cyrene,” Phainon whispered, his sobs beginning to quiet. His best friend. The girl he loved and cherished the most. His pillar. If only he hadn’t been powerless that day, he could’ve saved her. He could’ve saved his mom, his dad. He could’ve saved everyone.

What a Deliverer he was. He didn’t deserve the title. He didn’t deserve anything-companionship, kindness.

Love.

He didn’t deserve to live. Fate was cruel to let him live while everyone burned all around him.

Yet, here he was, destined to bear Kephale’s Core Flame. Destined to carry the world upon his shoulders, just like the World-Bearing Titan, without asking any questions. It wasn’t just his destiny, it was his duty.

Hah, fate really was cruel.

But now, he needed to get that clip from Mydei. The urge to hold it in his arms and hug it like it was some huge Chimera plushie was strong.

He sniffed, wiped his eyes, and was about to get up before he felt something warm wrap around him. Not burning like the sun, but gentle like a campfire. His head was tucked into the crook of someone’s neck, and he was being rocked back and forth. He didn’t want to open his eyes, he was scared of what he might see. But then he heard someone whisper something in his ear. He couldn’t make out everything that was said, except for the very last line. The last string of words resonated deep within him, and once it registered, he started to sob again, softer now, and nestled closer into the warmth that was so inviting. Into the warmth that invited him with open arms.

To say Mydei started to panic was an understatement. He expected Phainon’s reaction, but he didn’t think he'd react that badly!

One moment he was fine (or as fine as he could be), and the next he was a sobbing mess on the floor, yelling gibberish. All because of the clip in his hand that confirmed his suspicions.

This was no ordinary clip, and the memories he saw were enough evidence to point to the owner of it.

“Phainon!” He called, running up to the broken man and faltering a bit in his steps. How should he approach this? If he made any sudden movements, he’d startle the man further. He had to walk up to him slowly. What about touching him? Should he…

Ugh, fuck it. He always acted on his instincts and he wasn’t going to stop now.

Mydei crouched and crept up slowly. One wrong move and there was no telling what the Deliverer might do. He had to stay calm- for Phainon’s sake.

He placed an arm on Phainon’s shoulder and gently squeezed it. When he didn’t react, he pulled him into a hug, tucking his head under his chin. “Hey, Phainon?”

No response. Well, that was to be expected.

His body shook in his arms, and it hurt. It hurt so much to see him like this. Phainon was a ray of sunshine, a beacon of hope who always had a smile on his face. A kind-hearted soul who helped everyone in the Holy City. To see him like this now… Mydei had to calm him down. And the best way to calm him down was to talk to him.

“Phainon. I don’t know if you can hear me, but I need you to listen to me, please. I…I have some things to tell you.

“First of all, I’m so sorry for what I did. I didn’t know it was Cyrene’s pin. If I had known, I would’ve waited to give it back to you. I hope you can forgive me.

“I understand your grief. I understand it better than you realize. A home destroyed, comrades gone forever. You lost everything that meant the world to you, and I did as well. You couldn’t save them, and neither could I save my people. Let it all out, Phainon. Shed your grief. Mourn properly, for all tears are not a sign of weakness.”

Phainon’s sobs started to quiet down again, and Mydei smiled–it was working! He was getting to him. At least, he thinks he is.

You’re strong, Phainon. Stronger and braver than you realize. You’ve faced so much and came out standing when most would have fallen. Remember, Aedes Elysiae will never be forgotten as long as you’re still here. Everyone- your friends, your family, they all live in your hearts. They’ll always be a part of you, just like how we will always be here for you. Aglaea, Lady Tribbie and Trinnon, Castorice, Hyacine, even that scholar Anaxa. Me as well. You will never have to be alone.”

“Then, in a small act of boldness—if it could even be called that—he leaned forward and whispered into his ear, "I’m proud of you. And I know Cyrene would be proud if she could see the man you’ve become today. Everything you’ve done was not in vain.”

Mydei heard Phainon gasp, and all of a sudden, he felt a weird pressure on his chest. Phainon’s chin was resting there, eyes wide open, and quite red and puffy. He placed a hand under his chin and let his thumb graze his cheek. “Mydei?” he rasped.

“I’m here.” He tucked his head back to its usual resting spot. “I won’t let you go.”

“Thank you,” Phainon whispered. “I…Can you please…”

Mydei didn’t have to say anything and handed the clip to Phainon, who gripped it with such force his knuckles were slowly turning red. Mydei reached out and rubbed the spot gently. “Hey, don’t do that,” he said, his voice low.

“I’m worried that it might disappear under my palms.”

“It won’t. I can guarantee that.”

“But still.” He snuggled further. “I guess you recognize this.”

“It took me a while,” Mydei admitted. “My mind was eating me away. It was only after your outburst did I realize it belonged to Cyrene. The hair should’ve been a dead giveaway for me.”

Phainon laughed dryly. “At least you remembered. If you’re curious to know, I was the one who made this.”

Mydei felt his jaw slacken. Phainon cackled. “Wait, so it was you!? ”

“Surprised, Your Highness?”

“You can’t even fasten your cloak without looking like you fought it and lost. Since when did you have such nimble fingers?”

“I admit I’m a bit rusty now,” Phainon said, chuckling. “But I did have an eye for jewelry. It’s all thanks to my mom, really. She had a bunch of stuff in her room. Despite living in a village, we weren’t in complete misery. It took me a long time to make it. My mom offered to help, but being the stubborn child I was, I kept refusing. Maybe if I had, I would’ve finished it a whole lot sooner.”

“You’re still stubborn at times,” Mydei retorted.

Phainon rolled his eyes. “Look who’s calling the kettle black. Also, I never said I wasn’t stubborn.”

“Well then, let me rephrase that-you’re more stubborn than I.”

“Now that’s a lie, Mydei, and I can list a few examples. For instance, back at Maemoreal Market-”

“Ack! Ok, shut up and cry Deliverer,” Mydei groaned, shoving his palm into his face. Phainon cackled, hiding his face in his chiton. He sighed and stroked his hair. “But, putting aside everything we just said now, I meant everything I said before. I don’t think you’ll understand it now-you never do, but I hope one day it finally clicks in that pretty little brain of yours.”

“So you do think I’m pretty.”

“Ugh, shut up! Why do I even bother with you?”

“Because you love me🎶.”

“Unfortunately,” Mydei sighed. “So, what do you want to do? Do you want to leave and go back to Okhema or stay here for a bit?”

Phainon hummed and tightened his hold on him. He closed his eyes and uttered, “Stay here. I don’t think I’m strong enough to stand at the moment.”

“You know, I could carry you back.”

“You’d actually do that for me?”

“No.”

“You’re no fun.”

“But I could make a throne using my blood crystals and add some wheels.”

“Your Highness-”

“Phainon.”

“Your Royal Pompousness! How do you even sit on that thing? It’s uncomfortable as fuck.”

“You’re such a brat.”

“I’m your brat.”

“A tragedy indeed.”

“Mydei?”

“Yes?”

“Thank you,” Phainon said, locking eyes with Mydei and smiling. “I don’t think I would’ve even come here if it weren’t for you. Coming back here alone…I know I’d lose myself in my grief. I’m grateful that you’re my anchor.”

Mydei huffed and looked away, his ears burning, but deep down he was practically glowing at Phainon’s words. Of course, being the prideful demi-god he is, he’d never admit it.

But.

One day.

“You’re such a sappy idiot.”

Phainon laughed and didn’t say anything more. After all, there wasn’t anything that needed to be said now. They had each other, broken, but healing.

They’d never be the same, Phainon especially. Mydei knows he can’t always be there for him, that’s why he asked Chartonus to look after him. But, after witnessing what happened today, he figured it’d be best to come back once in a while, or at least text him during his few moments of rest.

For now, he’ll continue to hold him as he sheds away the remaining tears. He made a promise to never leave Phainon, and he intended to keep it.

(And in the after hours of Amphoreus’ Golden Age, in the ruins of the Capital of Might stood a King and a Black Robed Warrior. Golden ichor was spilt everywhere, pooling from the gaping wound where a sword laid buried deep in the king's chest. The swordmaster sobbed, cradling the man’s body as tears fell onto his face. His mask lay discarded near his feet. “Why,” he cried, his voice echoing off the walls. “Why does it have to end like this?”

“Because,” the king replied, weakly lifting his arm to caress his cheek, “That is our fate. It… cannot be changed. Thank you for putting me out of…my misery.”

The swordmaster wept terribly as the light faded from the king's eyes, knowing that Thanatos had finally accepted his beloved. Knowing he’d finally be able to rest in peace.)

EXTRA CHAPTER!!! I know some of you guys wanted some behind-the-scenes, so here's behind-the-scene no 1!

It's the infamous cooking scene lmao

"Oh fuck."

"Oh, oh shit oh shit oh shit it's scorching!"

"Uhhh, is it supposed to be like that?"

Phainon yelped as the pancake flew out of the pan and straight into the garbage bin, like the universe was giving him a sign to quit while he was at it. It was taunting him, whispering in its eerie voice that there was no way he'd be able to make a wonderful, delicious, and mouth-watering dish for the man he cared about.

If slamming his head into the wall would knock him out and end the chaos, he was about two seconds from trying it.

Propped up against the wall on the counter was the cookbook that the Chrysos Heirs used to cook their meals. Surprisingly (but not really), the book belonged to Mydei, who wrote down all the recipes he learned from his time leading the Kremnoan Detachment, bound the pages together, and stored them in the private kitchen for the Heirs to use. Over time, the others added their own recipes on the blank pages the prince left for them to scribble on.

And the recipes were admittedly good. Aglaea, Lady Tribbie, Trianne, and Trinnon had come up with a whole collection of oatmeal-based dishes that Phainon had initially assumed would be soggy and unappetizing, but they turned out to be anything but. Hyacine had also compiled a set of healthy meals packed with vegetables, proteins, and fiber that were perfect for days when no one felt like cooking anything extravagant. Castorice's recipes were more on the simpler side, but they were just as enjoyable. As for Phainon, well...

He was-

"OH FUCK OH SHIT AHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHHH!!!"

Phainon screamed like a banshee as he hurled the now-smoking pan into the sink, while trying not to scorch his fingers accidentally. He slammed the tap on full blast, muttering something about how battling Titankin was far better than mixing a bunch of random stuff as the flames hissed in protest. For fuck sake, he was making flipping pancakes! And he was following Mydei’s recipe to a T!

Well, no wonder he was banned from the kitchen. He couldn't even boil milk to save his life.

The last time he had been in here, he had tried to make a simple sandwich he could munch on after his spar, and that ended... disastrous, to say the least. After Aglaea saw the mess (she was alerted by the strong sense of something burning), she permanently banned him from ever entering the kitchen unless there was someone in there to supervise him.

It was a good thing no one decided to stop by to grab a snack, lest he be murdered and prematurely end the Flame Chase Journey, and knowing Aglaea, she’d probably prefer sacrificing the entire journey over letting him ruin another frying pan.

Great, Mydei was going to be here in an hour or two, and he had only a single pancake that looked edible on the plate, batter covering almost every inch of the kitchen, the sink overfilling with burnt kitchenware, and scorched pancakes all over the floor and ceiling. He had to make two stacks of pancakes and clean the mess he made before anyone saw him. Argh

The things he does for love. Mydei better appreciate his hard work!

Extra scene no 2! This time from Mydei's POV (it connects with Chapter 5)

Also I once again had to use the Yoda speak translator for Chartonus 😭😭

The coast was clear.

No Phainon in sight. Good. At least Mydei didn’t have to worry about ducking into suspicious alleyways just to avoid him. He wasn’t sure where he was, but oh well, does that matter now?

He walked through the market holding a bunch of parchments in his hand, nodding at those who greeted him and occasionally stopping to smile and ruffle the hair of children who stumbled over in excitement. The Entry Hour was about to pass, and the sun shone over his head. Sometimes, Mydei found himself wondering how summer in Okhema would be if the Dawn Device had a regulator that adjusted both the heat and light. But it wasn’t like he could walk up to Kephale and demand that, and he was fairly certain the device didn’t have any buttons to fiddle with.

Whatever. The weather never bothered him. He has seen worse.

Mydei passed by the Janus Device and strolled into the place he was looking for- Chartonus Smithy.

He booked an appointment with the Mountain-Dweller a while back, and it took a while since both of them were busy with stuff, but they were finally able to settle on a date for Chartonus to take his request. It was also convenient that Phainon happened to be out of town. It seemed the stars were finally aligning in his favor.

Chartonus was busy pounding away on what appeared to be a claymore when Mydei arrived, sweat covering his body from the heat of the flames. Tum and Siskel were standing at the edge of the forge, chatting away with some customers. He checked the time just to make sure he wasn't early or late- 12 pm.

He was right on time.

"Chartonus!" Mydei called out, waving his free hand to catch his attention. The other two Dwellers turned at the sound of his voice, offering small nods of acknowledgment before resuming their conversation. Chartonus paused mid-swing, the hammer still raised in his hand, and looked up with a grunt. "Prince Mydeimos. Came on time, you did. You'd be late, I thought."

"Since when was I ever late?" asked Mydei with a smirk. He was the Crown Prince of Castrum Kremnos. He was never late for anything. "Are you busy right now?"

"Almost finished with this weapon, I am," Chartonus said, gesturing at the blade. "Done I once am, with your commission, we shall begin. Bring any designs, did you?"

Mydei placed the parchments on the free table. "They're right here. Took me a while to settle on how I wanted them to look, bit I think the overall design came out well."

"Them?" Chartonus tilted his head.

"Ahh." How did Mydei forget to tell him when they last met? "Yeah. Apologies for not telling you earlier, it slipped my mind, but I want you to forge two weapons this time. Is that ok with you? I can pay double if needed."

Chartonus pounded the claymore one last time before setting it and his hammer aside to look at the blueprint. He grabbed the nearest one, unfurled it, and without even taking a proper look at it, he blurted out, "This weapon is for you, not, is it?"

He showed the parchment to Mydei, who barked out a laugh. Of course, a master blacksmith such as himself would be able to find out. "Sharp eyes, Chartonus. You'd be right- it isn't for me. And since you got that right, can you guess who it's for?"

"Easy to figure out, that is, for dressed to reflect the sun, who else in Okhema is? And I know for a fact you would commission a weapon for just anyone, not Prince Mydeimos."

So, even Chartonus figured it out. Well, no matter. "Check out the other design."

And check he did. Chartonus took his time examining every detail, occasionally jotting notes in the margins. They went back and forth over the design, starting with the bow, adjusting its curvature, grip, and draw weight—before moving on to the sword, where the discussion got even more intense.

"You add a moon want to?"

“His sword and the bow are already sun-themed,” Mydei replied with a shrug. “I thought something contrasting might give it more… balance.”

By the time they were finished, Action Hour was well underway, and the streets buzzed with activity. People clustered outside restaurants, enjoying lunch under the open sky, the scent of grilled meats and spiced vegetables drifting through the air. Mydei’s stomach gave a quiet grumble—he was definitely getting hungry. He was willing to bet Chartonus was, too. It was time to wrap this up.

He gave the blueprints one last satisfied nod and slid them across the table, along with a pouch. "I guess that'll be all then. I'll leave the rest to your magic, Chartonus."

"Start working on these as soon as I can, I will," said Chartonus, grabbing the paper and taking it inside.  "By when do you need them?"

"Finish them at your own pace and let me know a week in advance. I’ll find a way to evade Phainon... somehow.”

"Sounds good. In that case, you later, Prince Mydeimos, I shall see."

"I'll see you later too, Chartonus."

And with that, Mydei all but ran to the nearest restaurant to munch on some meat and honey cakes.

Hyacine sighed, tossing and turning restlessly on her bed. The wind blew gently through her open window, cooling the room with a soft breeze. Her hair, no longer tied in its usual pigtails, was strewn across the pillow in loose waves. Her uniform lay crumpled over the back of a chair, replaced now by a set of loose-fitting pajamas that hung comfortably on her frame. Beside her rested Ica, who was snoring softly and letting out little chirps that would normally make her giggle. Not today, sadly.

How long has it been since she, De, and the soldiers returned from their expedition? One? Two? Even three? She was supposed to be back at the Grove, writing down a report for the Twilight Courtyard and telling Professor Anaxa about the whole ordeal, but she couldn't find it in herself to get up. Her body was still smarting from healing so many people at once. She was banned from entering the infirmary by both Lady Aglaea and Lady Tribbie (apparently under strict orders from De and the two ladies themselves) until she was fully rested and able to stand on her own two feet without collapsing from sheer exhaustion. And...she couldn't find it in herself to argue back.

So, after a short talk with Mydei, she had found herself trudging back to her room and all but collapsed onto the bed. Little Ica fluttered anxiously around her, chirping in concern before finally settling at her side, nuzzling into the crook of her arm, letting out tiny bursts of his healing power. Hyacine smiled and carefully ruffled his mane before pulling him close and drifting off to sleep.

That was hours ago. Now, she was itching to put her hands to good use. Her body was brimming with excess energy she wanted to get rid of eagerly. Bubbles were drifting through the air, emerging from the mini bath, popping as they touched the ceiling. She couldn't just leave her room and go to the sickbay, for she knew Lady Aglaea would undoubtedly be there with her golden threads. In fact, she'd bet her threads should be strung all over her room by now, monitoring her every move like a network of living security cameras.

So boring!

Hyacine carefully stood up, careful not to jostle Ica, and covered his tiny body with the cover. If she wasn’t allowed to go anywhere that required using her powers, she might as well go outside and get some fresh air. That wasn’t a violation of any rules now, was it?

She walked over to her door, slipped on her shoes, and stepped outside, locking it behind her with a soft click. Ica could take care of himself, but she figured it'd be better if he got a few more minutes of rest. He deserved it after all for healing her.

The corridor was long and lit by the warm glow of the Dawn Device, its golden rays streaming through the tall windows and painting soft patterns on the floor. It led straight to the balcony where Hyacine would regularly sit and watch the city go on about their day. She may reside in the courtyard, but Lady Aglaea always wanted her to have a comfortable time when she was in Okhema. Plus, she oftentimes found herself coming back again and again when stress got to her.

She carefully sat down on the recliner and lay down, grabbing a book from the table. A bunch of romance novels that Castorice recommended were on the table- nothing too spicy (she'd rather take on the Black Tide herself instead of reading two people doing the goddamn tango!) but something to keep her entertained. The book she snagged looked like it was on the more comedic side. It was titled 'How to Hate You (And Fail Miserably).'

'Why does it remind me of two people..." Hyacine murmured, then shrugged her shoulders, brushing the thought aside. She was pretty sure it was just a coincidence.

..

.....

........

.........

Ok, it was not a coincidence. It certainly was not a coincidence!

It looked like whoever wrote this had Snowy and De in mind because the characters sounded exactly like them. No changes, no embellishments, nothing whatsoever. Now that Hyacine thought about it... did that count as copyright infringement?

Well, at least she was kicking her feet and squealing in joy. And she immediately got up to lock the balcony door. If she was going to read this, it's best to do it in secret...and maybe hunt down the author and ask for more.

It'll be her little secret. And Ica's.

The scent of metal hung heavy in the air as Okhema's two greatest warriors clashed in the training field, trading blow after blow under the morning sun. The sharp ring of Phainon’s sword striking against Mydei’s gauntlets reverberated across the stone walls like thunder cracking through a battlefield.

The soldiers from the Kremnoan Detachment watched with bated breath, eagerly cheering on their Crowned Prince and their Deliverer as their duel raged on. Mydei was quietly glad to see how they’d warmed up to Phainon over the years- sparring with him on occasion, and even helping the younger recruits with their swordplay. There was a time when he was worried if he had made the wrong move when he brought his people to the Holy City, but seeing how far they've come, he was proud.

Usually, when he and Phainon had one of their sparring sessions, they'd clear the arena lest they accidentally hurt someone, but the youngsters practically begged both of them to watch, claiming that they'd learn faster and better if they saw the 'pros' fighting. It just so happened that the other members of the detachment were conveniently at the baths at the time and overheard what the kids were saying. It didn’t take long before they joined in, begging the youngsters as well.

At first, Mydei got a bit frustrated and pinched the bridge of his nose, fully prepared to lecture them. They all knew how intense his and Phainon’s spars could get, and he didn’t want anyone standing too close. He wasn’t about to risk someone getting hurt just because they wanted front-row seats to a brawl.

Phainon, however, had merely shrugged and said, “Why not?” in the most infuriatingly casual tone imaginable, and it almost sent Mydei into a fit right then and there. He was this close to punching the Deliverer in the face and threatening him with a duel ban until he shot him those goddamn puppy eyes that made everyone's knees weak, and he found himself reluctantly agreeing. At least the children were happy after that.

(He still punched Phainon in the stomach after they left.)

Now, he was focused on beating the idiot, taking the offensive and pushing him into a corner. Phainon was aggressive, more so than usual and met every strike with fierce, unrelenting force. At one point, Phainon nearly sent him tumbling with a well-placed blow, and Mydei only managed to stay upright by planting his feet and digging his heel into the ground. Was it because of the crowd? He wasn't sure.

Regardless, it had been nearly three hours, and it was almost time for lunch. The restaurant they usually went to ran out of their honey cakes fast, and Mydei was not having it-he was going to do whatever it took to end this battle as fast as he could so he could drag his sorry ass and make him buy his favorite pastry and the entirety of their lunch (well, that was their bet this time.)

So, he shifted, exposing his side, and just as he predicted, Phainon saw the opening and lunged straight for him...

Only for Mydei to slam his elbow into Phainon’s back, knocking him to the ground with a thud. He barely gave him a second to recover as he towered over him, grabbed the sword before Phainon could, and pressed the blade near his throat.

The crowd went silent, save for their heavy breathing. The light from the Dawn Device shone overhead, casting long shadows across the arena floor and glinting off the steel of their weapons. Sweat drenched them both, soaking their clothes and clinging to their skin. Mydei leaned until he was at eye level and whispered into his ear, "Do you yield?"

Phainon huffed. "If I gave up now, this would be the shortest spar we’ve ever had. I’d be disgracing our ten-day-long battle."

"You'd only be disgracing it if I say so," Mydei replied, and stepped aside and held out his hand. "And I say you aren't. So don't worry your pretty little head over it, Phainon. You did well."

Mydei pulled him to his feet, and the crowd around them erupted into cheers and applause. Phainon giggled, brushing off the dust as he let go of Mydei’s hand and gave an exaggerated bow to their audience, causing him to roll his eyes. Ever the showman that stupid Deliverer...

Unfortunately, it was the same man he liked.

So, without further warning, he grabbed Phainon's arm and dragged him to the baths, ignoring his excessive whining. They still had to wash themselves before heading for lunch, and he was hungry as hell.
